items.title: Minor salivary gland biopsies in childhood-onset Sjögren's disease show greater inflammation and more frequent fibrotic changes than in adult-onset Sjögren's disease.
items.abstract: To provide the first histopathological characterization of minor salivary gland (MSG) biopsies in childhood-onset Sjögren's disease (cSjD) in comparison with adult Sjögren's disease (SjD). MSG biopsies obtained by eighteen consecutive children fulfilling the 2016 ACR/EULAR classification criteria for SjD and 55 consecutive adult SjD patients were analysed. Clinical features, ESSDAI, ESSPRI, and salivary gland histopathology were collected according to EULAR standards, including focus score (FS), lymphoepithelial lesions (LELs), and ectopic germinal centers (GCs) by immunohistochemistry. Compared with adults, children showed a more inflammatory phenotype. Recurrent parotid swelling was significantly more frequent in cSjD (38.9% vs. 5.5%, p = 0.0015), whereas xerostomia and xerophthalmia predominated in adults (p < 0.0001 for both). Palpable purpura was more common in children (44.4% vs. 1.8%, p < 0.0001), while fatigue and myalgia were rare (p = 0.0058 and p < 0.0001, respectively). Rheumatoid factor was more prevalent in cSjD (77.7% vs. 30.9%, p = 0.0072), whereas anti-SSA antibodies were less frequent (p = 0.0029). ESSDAI scores were higher (p = 0.0001) and ESSPRI lower (p < 0.0001) in children, reflecting greater systemic inflammation but lower subjective symptom burden. Pediatric biopsies exhibited higher FS than adults (median 3.4 vs. 1.0, p = 0.0002), together with more frequent GCs (44.4% vs. 5.5%, p = 0.00034), LELs (61.1% vs. 5.5%, p < 0.0001), and fibrotic changes (66.7% vs. 27.3%, p = 0.0048). Quantitative immunohistochemistry further showed significantly increased CD3 and CD20 lymphocytic infiltrates in cSjD biopsies, together with an increased CD20/(CD20 + CD3) proportion (all p < 0.0001). MSG biopsies in cSjD show a more inflammatory, lymphoid-organizing B-enriched phenotype, with more frequent fibrosis than in adults. These findings are in keeping with previous observations in pediatric parotid tissue and highlight frequent fibrotic remodelling alongside marked inflammation despite shorter disease duration in children.

items.title: [Adrenal ganglioneuroma as an incidentaloma in a patient with Sjögren's syndrome].
items.abstract: Ganglioneuroma is a benign, non-functional tumor, most of which are asymptomatic and discovered incidentally through imaging studies or at autopsy. We present the case of a 47-year-old woman with Sjögren's syndrome. Computed tomography scan of the abdomen showed an ovoid tumor with well-defined borders, measuring 11 x 8 cm, located in the left adrenal gland. Robotassisted adrenalectomy was performed, and microscopic examination revealed a mature ganglioneuroma. Although imaging studies such as computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging are effective in the diagnostic approach to adrenal tumors, histopathological evaluation is essential for definitive diagnosis. El ganglioneuroma es un tumor benigno no funcional, la mayoría de ellos son asintomáticos y descubiertos de forma incidental a través de estudios de imagen o en estudios de autopsia. Presentamos el caso de una mujer de 47 años con síndrome de Sjögren. Una tomografía computarizada de abdomen mostró un tumor ovoide de bordes bien definidos de 11 x 8 cm, localizado en la glándula suprarrenal izquierda. Se realizó adrenalectomía asistida por robot y el estudio microscópico reveló un ganglioneuroma maduro. Aun cuando los estudios de imagen como la tomografía computarizada y la resonancia magnética son útiles en el abordaje diagnóstico de tumores suprarrenales, la evaluación histopatológica es esencial para el diagnóstico definitivo.

items.title: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease: immune profiling and correlation of immune cells with pulmonary function in SSc-ILD.
items.abstract: Connective tissue diseases (CTDs) frequently involve the lungs, with CTD-associated interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD) representing a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, yet the immunopathological mechanisms remain incompletely defined. This study characterized immune profiles in CTD-ILD and their association with pulmonary function impairment, focusing on systemic sclerosis-associated ILD (SSc-ILD). This single-center retrospective study enrolled 217 CTD-ILD patients, 100 healthy controls, and 25 idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) patients. Peripheral lymphocyte subsets, immunoglobulins, complements, and cytokines were assessed using flow cytometry and immunoturbidimetry. Lung function was evaluated by standard spirometry and gas transfer tests. Compared to healthy controls, lymphocyte counts were reduced in all ILD subtypes, lowest in polymyositis/dermatomyositis (PM/DM)-ILD. In SSc-ILD, T cell and helper T cell (Th) percentages were significantly elevated (76.2% and 49.39%, respectively). Complement C3 was lower in Sjögren's syndrome (SS)-ILD (889.92 vs. 965.49 mg/L), and C4 was significantly lower in SSc-ILD (196.74 vs. 226.70 mg/L) versus controls. SSc-ILD patients with higher Th cell proportions exhibited worse pulmonary function, with expiratory reserve volume (ERV) falling 57.21%, maximal vital capacity (VC max) 18.81%, functional residual capacity (FRC) 19.64%, forced vital capacity (FVC)17.93%, and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) 20.28%. Continuous correlation analysis further confirmed significant negative correlations between Th cell proportions and ERV, FRC, and PCO 2 . Peripheral blood immune profiling revealed distinct abnormalities across CTD-ILD subtypes. Peripheral Th cell expansion is strongly associated with lung function decline in SSc-ILD, highlighting the potential of Th cells as biomarkers of disease progression in SSc-ILD.

items.title: A Multi-Axis Plantar Load Measurement Platform for the Assessment of Foot Disorders: Comparison of Patients With Psoriatic Arthritis to a Healthy Control Cohort.
items.abstract: Accurate assessment of plantar loading, including shear forces, is crucial for understanding foot pathologies such as dactylitis in psoriatic arthritis (PsA). Existing devices predominantly measure plantar pressures, neglecting important shear stresses which may initiate dactylitis. This study presents a novel multi-axis plantar load measurement platform to address this gap. The study utilised a newly developed plantar load measurement system, comprising a Hall-effect-based magnetic sensing array, custom data logging electronics, and tailored data processing software. The system's efficacy was evaluated in a pilot feasibility study involving patients with PsA with no, current, or previous dactylitis, and healthy controls. Participants walked barefoot on the platform, capturing plantar shear and pressure data. Shear stresses were notably higher in the second to fourth rays compared to other regions, particularly in the left foot, aligning with the hypothesis that repetitive local trauma might initiate dactylitis in PsA. However, no consistent differences in stresses were observed between diagnostic groups, likely due to small sample sizes and gait alterations associated with pain. A marked asymmetry was observed between the right and left feet, suggesting dominant-foot placement effects. The new platform demonstrates potential clinical utility in capturing comprehensive foot-loading profiles, including critical shear stresses previously under-assessed. Although the current pilot study was limited in number, the results support the theory that local mechanical stresses may contribute to PsA-related dactylitis. Future larger-scale studies are needed to clarify these findings and overcome limitations related to altered gait patterns due to foot pain.

items.title: Metabolic gatekeepers shape immune cell function in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Immune cell function is tightly coupled to cellular metabolism, with glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation, and amino acid and lipid metabolism governing activation, differentiation, survival, and effector responses. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), an autoimmune disease characterized by destructive joint inflammation, metabolic checkpoints have emerged as critical regulators of immune-cell behavior and drivers of tissue pathology. RA CD4+ T cells undergo profound metabolic reprogramming: glycolysis is suppressed, and glucose is redirected into the pentose phosphate pathway, resulting in NADPH accumulation, reduced ROS levels, and a highly reductive intracellular environment. Concurrent defects in mitochondrial DNA repair and electron transport chain function compromise mitochondrial fitness, leading to NAD+ depletion, altered tricarboxylic acid cycle activity, and metabolic exhaustion. The resulting accumulation of citrate and acetyl-CoA promotes lipogenesis and protein acetylation, driving membrane remodeling, tissue invasiveness, and proinflammatory effector functions. Depletion of oxaloacetate and aspartate limits NAD+ regeneration, inducing endoplasmic reticulum expansion and enhanced tumor necrosis factor production. Defective lysosomal coordination of AMPK and mTORC1 signaling uncouples energy sensing from anabolic programs, enabling cellular activation and proliferation despite metabolic insufficiency. Macrophage fate and function are similarly shaped by metabolic state. In synovial macrophages, GLUD1-dependent glutamine oxidation sustains mitochondrial respiration and ATP production, enabling survival under nutrient-deprived conditions while promoting antigen presentation. Conversely, metabolic stress in MerTK+ macrophages activates the NAD+ hydrolase SARM1, triggering NAD+ depletion, mitochondrial collapse, and PANoptotic cell death. Together, these findings identify NAD+ availability, mitochondrial fitness, and organelle-based signaling as central metabolic gatekeepers linking bioenergetic stress to immune-cell dysfunction and chronic inflammation in RA.

items.title: [IgG4-related disease presenting with involvement of the eyes, pituitary gland and nervous system: A case report].
items.abstract: To report a case of IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) involving the eyes, pituitary gland, dura mater and temporal region simultaneously. The patient was a 55-year-old middle-aged male with a protracted course of more than 13 years. The main clinical manifestations included swelling of the left eye accompanied by exophthalmos, which gradually worsened, and progressive visual deterioration. Imaging examinations revealed multiple pseudotumorous masses in the bilateral extraconal spaces (superior to the bilateral superior rectus muscles and inferior to the bilateral inferior rectus muscles) and the left optic nerve sheath area, pseudotumorous thickening of the bilateral temporal dura mater, sellar nodules, as well as pseudotumorous thickening of the muscular tissues in the left temporal and maxillofacial regions. Laboratory tests showed elevated serum IgG4 levels. Pathohistological biopsy of the ocular tissue demonstrated lymphoid hyperplasia accompanied by whorled or storiform proliferative fibrous tissue, formation of lymphoid follicles, and plasma cell infiltration. Immunohistochemical staining was positive for IgG4, with the ratio of IgG4-positive plasma cells to total IgG-positive plasma cells exceeding 70%. After treatment with hormones combined with immunosuppressants, the lesions in these areas shrank and some disappeared. Therefore, the comprehensive diagnosis was IgG4-RD.

items.title: [Systemic sclerosis with anti-human neutrophil cytoplasm antibody associated vasculitis: A case report].
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is an autoimmune disease involving microvessels and a wide range of connective tissues. Anti-human neutrophil cytoplasm antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) is a primary, systemic necrotizing small vasculitis. The coexistence of AAV and SSc is rare. We report a case of SSc combined with AAV complicated with alveolar hemorrhage, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, and cerebral hemorrhage. The patient was a 56-year-old woman with a 20-year history of Raynaud phenomenon, skin sclerosis on the fingertip and face. She developed dry cough for 1 year and shortness of breath after activity for 1month. Blood routine test showed moderate anemia, blood biochemistry showed renal function damage, and urine routine test showed positive urine protein and occult blood. Immunological examination showed that anti-topoisomerase Ⅰ (anti-SCL-70) antibody was positive. Lung CT showed interstitial fibrosis in both lower lungs. Systemic sclerosis and chronic renal injury were diagnosed and she was treated with low-dose prednisone and nifedipine. During the treatment, the patient developed rapidly progressive renal insufficiency, immunological indicator showed positive anti-myeloperoxidase antibody (MPO), and renal pathology suggested crescentic glomerulonephritis. The renal damage was considered to be caused by vasculitis, and the diagnosis was modified as systemic sclerosis complicated with AAV, with crescentic nephritis and interstitial lung disease. She was treated with methylprednisolone 500 mg. One day later, the patient developed hemoptysis, alveolar hemorrhage was considered, and treatment was adjusted to methylprednisolone 1 g for 3 days, plasma exchange and cyclophosphamide. Three days later, she had vomiting coffee-colored gastric contents and melena. Gastrointestinal hemorrhage was considered, and methylprednisolone was reduced to 80 mg. Plasma exchange and cyclophosphamide treatment were continued, supplemented by acid suppression. The patient's condition was finally controlled, improved and discharged. One month later, the patient developed cough and sputum, and lung CT showed pulmonary infection. During anti-infection treatment, the patient developed gastrointestinal hemorrhage again, accompanied by cerebral hemorrhage, and finally died. This case shows that the incidence of SSc combined with AAV is dangerous, mainly with kidney involvement, manifested as crescents glomerulonephritis. When combined with alveolar hemorrhage, cerebral hemorrhage, the mortality rate is high. Clinicians should pay attention to it, early diagnosis and active treatment should be taken seriously.

items.title: [Seronegative rheumatoid arthritis combined with elbow pigmented villonodular synovitis: A case report].
items.abstract: We report a case of elbow pigmented villonodular synovitis (PVNS) combined with seronegative rheumatoid arthritis (SNRA) and review relevant literature to summarize the characteristics, treatment, and outcomes of this comorbidity. The patient was a 72-year-old female. She developed swelling and pain of the right elbow in 2002, and underwent surgical treatment. Postoperative histopathology confirmed PVNS. In 2007, she developed swelling and pain in the left elbow and underwent synovectomy, and synovectomy again yielded pathology consistent with PVNS. From 2021 onwards, she experienced recurrent bilateral knee pain and swelling. In June 2023, laboratory tests revealed markedly elevated inflammatory markers: C-reactive protein (CRP) 175.3 mg/L, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) 116 mm/h, hemoglobin 83 g/L, and platelet count 537×10 9 /L. Rheumatoid factor, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptideantibody, anti-keratin antibody, and anti-perinuclear factor were all negative. Right knee magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed severe degenerative changes, suprapatellar bursitis with large effusion, and ligamentous injuries. Given her prior PVNS history and knee MRI findings, right knee replacement was performed; however, intraoperatively no nodular or mass-like synovial proliferation was observed. Postoperative synovial pathology demonstrated massive chronic inflammatory cell infiltration, small vessel proliferation, and fibrinoid necrosis-findings typical of rheumatoid arthritis rather than PVNS. After surgery, the left knee continued to experience recurring pain and swelling. In April 2024, she developed swelling and pain in both wrists and right ankle joints. Ultrasound examinations showed synovial proliferation in the wrists, knees, ankles, and metatarsophalangeal joints, with abundant blood flow signals and bone erosion. The patient was diagnosed as SNRA combined with PVNS. Treatment with tocilizumab 400 mg intravenously monthly plus methotrexate 10 mg weekly was initiated. After three months, CRP decreased to 0.73 mg/L, ESR to 6 mm/h. A literature review using Wanfang, CNKI, and PubMed databases with keywords "rheumatoid arthritis" and "pigmented villonodular synovitis" identified only four previously reported cases of RA combined with PVNS. Including the present case, there were 5 cases (4 females, 1 male), the median age of PVNS onset was 45 (32.5-58.0) years. The knee was the most commonly affected joint (4/5 cases), followed by the elbow. PVNS preceded RA in two cases (by 3 and 12 years), rheumatoid arthritis (RA) preceded PVNS in two cases (by 3 and 15 years), and one case had simultaneous onset. Four of the five patients were seropositive for rheunatoid factor/anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody (RF/anti-CCP); only the index case was seronegative. All five patients underwent synovial resection; two (40%) experienced postoperative recurrence. In conclusion, the coexistence of PVNS and SNRA is extremely rare and poses diagnostic challenges due to overlapping clinical manifestations. Physicians should consider the possibility of RA when a patient with PVNS develops symmetric polyarthritis, and conversely, suspect concomitant PVNS when a patient with RA has persistent monoarticular symptoms uncontrolled by disease-modifying therapy. Synovial fluid analysis, MRI findings, and especially histopathological examination are crucial for differentiation. Early recognition and appropriate immunotherapy can significantly improve prognosis.

items.title: [Clinical characteristics and risk factors of patients with rheumatoid arthritis complicated with urinary tract infection].
items.abstract: To explore the clinical characteristics of urinary tract infection (UTI) in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), to evaluate the effects of different treatment regimens on the risk of UTI, and to identify independent risk factors for UTI complicated with RA. A retrospective cohort study was conducted. RA patients hospitalized in the Department of Rheumatology and Immunology, The First Affiliated Hospital of Baotou Medical College from September 2020 to September 2023 were enrolled. General clinical data, laboratory indicators and medication information of the patients were collected. Patients were divided into two groups according to the presence or absence of UTI for comparative analysis. Patients were grouped based on different treatment regimens received, and the proportions of UTI occurrence were compared among each group. The results of urine culture and drug susceptibility test in the RA patients with UTI were analyzed. Univariate and multivariate Logistic regression analyses were further performed to screen relevant factors for UTI in the RA patients, and the diagnostic value of combined indicators was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. A total of 196 RA patients were included, among whom 99 cases were complicated with UTI and 97 cases without UTI. Compared with the non-UTI group, the UTI group had higher proportions of female patients, patients aged ≥65 years, patients with RA disease duration ≥10 years, patients hospitalized for infection within the past two years, and patients with comorbidities (diabetes mellitus, hypertension, etc.). Peripheral blood leukocyte count, percentage of neutrophils, serum procalcitonin, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein level were elevated ( P < 0.05), while hemoglobin, percentage of lymphocytes and plasma albumin level were decreased ( P < 0.05). The RA patients were divided into four groups according to different treatment regimens: ①glucocorticoids (GCs) monotherapy group; ②conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) monotherapy group; ③csDMARDs combined with GCs group; ④ csDMARDs combined with biological DMARDs (bDMARDs)/ targeted synthetic DMARDs (tsDMARDs) group. The overall difference in UTI proportion among the four groups was statistically significant ( P < 0.001). After Bonferroni correction, the UTI proportion in group ① and group ③ was higher than that in group ② and group ④ (adjusted P < 0.05). GSs use was associated with increased UTI risk, and the risk of UTI showed an upward trend with the increase of daily dose. Multivariate Logistic regression analysis demonstrated that RA disease duration ≥10 years, previous hospitalization due to infection within the past two years, comorbid diabetes mellitus, and elevated disease activity score in 28 joints based on ESR (DAS28-ESR) were independent risk factors for UTI in the RA patients. The area under the ROC curve of the diagnostic model constructed with the above combined predictors was 0.82 (95% CI : 0.76-0.88), with a sensitivity of 0.67 and a specificity of 0.94. Gram-negative bacteria were the predominant pathogens in urine culture of the RA patients with UTI, among which Escherichia coli accounted for 67.71%. Among evaluable single-isolate bacterial strains with available drug-susceptibility results, the resistance rates to levofloxacin and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole were 65.4% and 52.8%, respectively. Clinical infection surveillance should be strengthened in RA patients. GCs should be rationally used on the premise of effective RA disease control, and bDMARDs/tsDMARDs therapy should be initiated timely according to disease status to reduce GCs exposure and minimize the risk of UTI. Meanwhile, antimicrobial agents should be selected in a standardized manner based on urine culture and drug susceptibility test results.

items.title: [Risk factors of carotid atherosclerosis in patients with rheumatoid arthritis].
items.abstract: To analyze the characteristics of lipid profile and the risk factors of carotid atherosclerosis (CAS) in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Subjects with 216 RA and 214 healthy controls, both without known cardiovascular disease (CVD), were included. CAS plaques were determined by color Doppler ultrasound. Lipid levels were compared between RA patients and healthy controls, and independent risk factors for CAS plaques in the RA patients were analyzed. (1) The total cholesterol (TC), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels were lower ( P < 0.001, P =0.001, P < 0.001), TC/HDL-C and LDL-C/HDL-C were higher ( P =0.003, P =0.009) in the RA group than in the healthy controls. (2) In RA group, TC and HDL-C were negatively correlated with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) ( r =-0.237, P =0.002; r =-0.351, P < 0.001), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) ( r =-0.210, P =0.006; r =-0.182, P =0.018); LDL-C was negatively correlated with NLR ( r =-0.200, P =0.009), triglyceride (TG) was negatively correlated with erythrocyte sedimentation rate ( r =-0.184, P =0.016), TC/HDL-C was positively correlated with hs-CRP and NLR ( r =0.286, P < 0.001; r =0.159, P =0.039), LDL-C/HDL-C was positively correlated with hs-CRP ( r =0.161, P =0.040). In patients with RA, HDL-C levels were higher, and TG and TC/HDL-C levels were lower in the group treated regularly with conventional synthetic disease modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) than without csDMARDs ( P =0.035, P =0.003, P =0.006). (3) The prevalence of CAS plaques in RA patients was 37.5%. Age, disease duration, prevalence of hypertension, prevalence of diabetes, LDL-C/HDL-C, homocysteine (Hcy) and hs-CRP levels were higher in the RA with plaque group than in the RA without plaque group (all P < 0.05). (4) Logistic regression showed that age ( OR =1.085, 95% CI : 1.045-1.128), disease duration ( OR =1.008, 95% CI : 1.003-1.014), diabetes ( OR =4.326, 95% CI : 1.606-11.655), and hs-CRP ( OR =1.022, 95% CI : 1.006-1.038) were independent risk factors for the presence of CAS plaques in the RA patients. Patients with RA are more likely to exhibit lipid metabolic abnormalities which are mainly manifested as low cholesterol levels (TC, LDL-C, HDL-C) and high lipid ratios (TC/HDL-C, LDL-C/HDL-C). Such disordered lipid profileis are associated with gender, inflammatory and drug therapy. Age, disease duration, inflammatory status, and diabetes are independent risk factors for CAS plaques in RA patients. Effective control of inflammatory status are important goals of RA management and may also be essential to delay the progression of atherosclerosis.

items.title: [Clinical characteristics of primary Sjögren syndrome with leukopenia].
items.abstract: To analyze the clinical characteristics of leukopenia in a large cohort of patients with primary Sjögren syndrome (pSS), to discuss its pathogenic mechanism, and to enhance clinicians ' understanding of the disease, and reduce missed diagnosis and misdiagnosis. A total of 401 inpatients and outpatients who were initially diagnosed with pSS at the Department of Rheumatology and Immunology, Ninth People' s Hospital, Shanghai Jiaotong University School of Medicine, from November 2019 to March 2023 were selected for this study. The clinical data and laboratory examinations of these patients were analyzed retrospectively. Of the 401 patients, 107 (26.68%) were complicated with blood leukopenia. The reasons for the first diagnosis were analyzed. The patients with leukopenia had a lower xerostomia and xerophthalmia (39.25% vs. 54.76%, P =0.006), but a higher incidence of fatigue (26.17% vs. 12.59%, P =0.001) and thrombocytopenia (11.21% vs. 2.72%, P =0.001) than those without leukopenia. There were no significant differences in arthralgia, oral ulcer, caries, chest tightness, asthma and anemia between the two groups ( P >0.05). The laboratory test indicators were analyzed. The patients with leukopenia had a higher prevalence of anti-SSA/Ro52+ (81.31% vs. 68.35%, P =0.040), anti-SSB+ (47.66% vs. 28.57%, P < 0.001), immunoglobulin G (IgG)+ (68.22% vs. 51.02%, P =0.002), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) elevation (67.29% vs. 41.32%, P =0.001), and thrombocytopenia (22.43% vs. 13.27%, P =0.026) than those without leukopenia. There were no significant differences in antinuclear antibody (ANA)+, anti-SSA/Ro60+, centromere protein B(CENP-B)+, rheumatoid factor (RF)+, and anemia between the two groups ( P >0.05). The positive rate of abnormal salivary gland ultrasound in pSS with leukopenia group was higher than that in normal group ( P =0.029). There was no significant difference in salivary flow rate, dry eye test and lip gland biopsy between the two groups ( P >0.05). The incidence of pSS combined with leukopenia and autoimmune hepatitis (10.28% vs. 3.40%, P =0.006) was higher than that of the normal group, and the incidence of interstitial pneumonia (16.82% vs. 14.97%, P =0.649), renal tubule acidosis (2.80% vs. 3.06%, P =0.649) and renal tubule acidosis (2.80% vs. 3.06%, P =0.893) were no significant differences between the two groups ( P >0.05). Analysis of the effect of antibody on leukopenia showed that the proportion of leukopenia was higher in anti-SSA/Ro52+ group (30.00% vs. 18.02%, P =0.015). The percentages of leukopenia (37.78% vs. 21.05%, P < 0.001), neutropenia (31.85% vs. 16.92%, P < 0.001) and lymphocytopenia (24.44% vs. 21.03%, P =0.001) in anti-SSB+ group were significantly higher than those in anti-SSB- group. In certain patients with pSS, leukopenia manifested as the initial clinical symptom, as opposed to the typically expected dry mouth and eyes. When compared to the group with normal leukocyte levels, the group of pSS patients with leukopenia demonstrated a higher susceptibility to fatigue symptoms and exocrine gland involvement. Additionally, this leukopenia group exhibited a higher rate of antibody positivity, increased disease activity, and a greater likelihood of developing liver disease complicated by autoimmunity. These findings underscore the need for heightened clinical attention.

items.title: [Explore the potential diagnostic markers of primary Sjögren syndrome by bioinformatics combined with machine learning].
items.abstract: To develop a diagnostic model for primary Sjögren syndrome (pSS) utilizing transcriptomics-based machine learning techniques, and to explore potential therapeutic targets. We selected patients diagnosed with pSS and control subjects with salivary gland samples from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database for transcriptome sequencing. This was complemented by methylation sequencing data, followed by weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) in conjunction with clinical data to identify candidate diagnostic genes. Subsequently, we refined the gene list using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), random forest (RF), Gaussian mixed model (GMM), and support vector machine (SVM). Ultimately, we constructed a composite diagnostic model for pSS employing SVM, neural networks (NN), Logistic regression (LR), decision trees (DT), adaptive boosting (AdaBoost), bootstrap aggregating (Bagging), random forest, and Naive Bayes classifiers, totaling eight distinct machine learning algorithms, and predicted drug targets. Through differential gene screening combined with WGCNA analysis of the GEO database, we identified 12 key genes. Further variable selection via machine learning techniques yielded four significant genes: VNN2 , NAPSB , SAMSN1 , and MS4A1 . The area under curve (AUC) values were calculated for each gene: AUC VNN2 =0.865, AUC NAPSB =0.896, AUC SAMSN1 =0.872, AUC MS4A1 =0.914, all demonstrating diagnostic relevance. We then employed these machine learning methods to construct a composite diagnostic model, and F1 score (the harmonic mean of precision and recall rate) was used to evaluate the prediction performance of each model in the internal test set. The top-performing models included those based on SVM polynomial kernel models, SVM linear kernel models, random forest approaches, and Naive Bayes classification as determined through ranking criteria based on AUC comparisons; notably, both SVM polynomial kernel models and linear kernel models exhibited superior AUC values compared with individual genes alone. The external validation set, SVM polynomial kernel function model in GSE159574, AUC=0.865 (95% CI : 0.728-1.000), sensitivity 0.812, specificity 0.846; The AUC of SVM polynomial kernel model in GSE173808, AUC=0.896 (95% CI : 0.797-0.996), the sensitivity was 0.778, and the specificity was 1.000. In order to facilitate clinical diagnosis, we verified that the AUC of the SVM polynomial kernel function model in the peripheral blood GSE84844 dataset was 0.827 (95% CI : 0.719-0.934), the sensitivity was 0.867, and the specificity was 0.767. Thus, our proposed model demonstrated robust diagnostic capability for pSS. Additionally, our investigation into potential drug targets indicated that these four identified genes served as targets for glucocorticoid therapies while curcumin emerged as a promising candidate agent in treating pSS. This research identifies VNN2 , NAPSB , SAMSN1 , and MS4A1 as specific biomarkers for diagnosing pSS, thereby enriching existing genetic markers relevant to diagnosis while establishing a reliable composite diagnostic framework which underscores the close association between methylation processes in the pathogenesis of pSS, offering novel insights into early diagnosis strategies along with prospective treatment avenues.

items.title: Thromboxane A2 receptor signalling amplifies osteoclastogenesis in rheumatoid arthritis through ACSL1 associated mitochondrial oxidative metabolism.
items.abstract: Activated platelets contribute to inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis, but how platelet-derived signals promote bone erosion remains poorly understood. Here we show that thromboxane A2, a major mediator released by activated platelets, promotes the formation of bone-resorbing osteoclasts through the thromboxane A2 receptor. Markers of thromboxane A2 biosynthesis are increased in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, while pharmacological inhibition or genetic loss of its receptor suppresses osteoclastogenesis in mouse cells and mice. Integrated molecular analyses reveal that thromboxane A2 receptor signalling supports osteoclastogenesis by increasing fatty acid oxidation and acetyl-coenzyme A supply needed for mitochondrial energy metabolism, involving peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1 beta, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma and acyl-coenzyme A synthetase long-chain family member 1. In male mice, receptor inhibition or genetic deletion reduces osteoclast accumulation and bone destruction. These findings identify thromboxane A2 signalling as a driver of inflammatory bone erosion and a potential therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis.

items.title: The spectrum of cardiovascular disease in systemic lupus erythematosus and rheumatoid arthritis: a nationwide case-control postmortem study.
items.abstract: To examine cardiovascular pathology in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) vs. population-based controls, and its association with cause of death. A case-control postmortem study was performed in Australia using the National Coronial Information System (2000-2025). SLE/RA cases were identified via keyword/ICD-10 code search. Controls were selected from motor vehicle accident deaths (3:1 ratio). Cardiovascular findings/histology were extracted from autopsy reports. Associations between SLE/RA and cardiovascular findings/outcomes using logistic regression (odds ratios (OR), 95% confidence intervals (CI)). 363 cases (240 RA&123 SLE) and 123 controls of similar age (cases 63y (IQR 53-72), vs. controls 59y (47-73), p=0.166) and sex (female 69% vs. controls 75%, p=0.235) were included. Adjusting for age, sex and BMI, myocardial fibrosis (SLE OR3.66, 95%CI2.00-6.72, p<0.001; RA OR3.96, 95%CI2.37-6.60, p<0.001), myocardial inflammation (SLE OR14.79, 95%CI3.35-65.37, p<0.001; RA OR6.35, 95%CI1.44-28.09, p=0.015) and cardiomegaly (SLE OR5.70, 95%CI2.99-10.86, p<0.001; RA OR3.50, 95%CI2.02-6.08, p<0.001) were more frequent in SLE and RA, as were coronary artery disease (CAD; SLE OR2.46, 95%CI1.34-4.51, p=0.004; RA OR2.56, 95%CI1.54-4.27, p<0.001) and microvascular disease (SLE OR10.28, 95%CI2.28- 46.31; RA OR6.74, 95%CI1.53-29.57, p=0.012). Associations between cardiovascular findings and SLE/RA status were strongest in under-60s, and persisted after adjusting for CAD. Cardiovascular death was associated with myocardial fibrosis (SLE OR2.35, 95%CI1.02-5.43, p=0.045; RA OR3.62, 95%CI1.81-7.27, p<0.001), cardiomegaly (SLE OR3.77, 95%CI1.71-8.27, p=0.001; RA OR2.52, 95%CI1.44-4.43, p=0.001) and CAD (SLE OR4.12, 95%CI1.76-9.66, p=0.001; RA OR12.71, 95%CI6.59-24.49, p<0.001); and microvascular disease (OR5.26, 95%CI1.40-19.77, p=0.014) and valvular pathology (OR2.68, 95%CI1.11-6.43, p=0.028) in SLE only. This unique dataset identified increased atherosclerotic, inflammatory and fibrotic cardiovascular disease in SLE and RA, particularly in younger individuals. These pathologies were frequently associated with cardiovascular death.

items.title: Patterns of NT-proBNP in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: We evaluated patterns of N-terminal prohormone of n-terminal brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP, a biomarker of cardiac disease) in SLE, and associations with demographic and clinical characteristics. We analyzed data from the McGill SLE Research Cohort, including yearly serum NTproBNP. We assessed prevalence of baseline elevated NT-proBNP (≥133 ng/L) , and associations with baseline variables: age, sex, race/ethnicity, age at SLE diagnosis, SLE duration, smoking, and SLE International Collaborating Clinics Damage Index. Patients were classified into four NT-proBNP patterns: abnormal at baseline and remaining abnormal; abnormal and normalizing; normal and becoming abnormal; normal and remaining normal. We compared baseline characteristics across patterns using multivariate logistic regressions. We studied 294 patients with ≥2 measurements. At baseline, 101 (34.4%) had elevated NT-proBNP. Higher levels were associated with older age at SLE diagnosis, longer SLE duration, cardiovascular damage, pulmonary hypertension, and renal damage. Of 101 individuals with abnormal baseline NT-proBNP, 79 (78.2%) remained abnormal. Of the 193 with normal baseline levels, 30 (15.5%) became abnormal. No patient with a baseline level ≥350 normalized to <133. High-risk patterns (abnormal-remaining-abnormal and normal-becoming-abnormal) were more likely to have cardiovascular damage (OR 3.90, 95% CI 1.49-12.5, renal damage (OR 2.87, 95% CI 1.61-5.51), and pulmonary hypertension (OR 32.0, 95% CI 4.59-651.1). Over one-third of SLE patients had abnormal baseline NT-proBNP; most (78%) remained abnormal. Over 15% of those with an initially normal value became abnormal. Higher levels were associated with age, SLE duration, and organ damage. Levels ≥350 ng/L did not normalize over our evaluation.

items.title: Cardiovascular Phenotypes in Women with Sjögren Disease: Hormonal, Immune, and Clinical Perspectives.
items.abstract: Sjögren disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disorder with a marked female predominance and an increasingly recognised, although incompletely characterised, cardiovascular (CV) burden. This review examines the biological, clinical, and gender-related determinants of CV involvement in women with SjD. We conducted a structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE covering the period from January 2010 to July 2026, supplemented by backward citation searching to identify relevant earlier studies. Original SjD-specific studies were prioritised, while systematic reviews, meta-analyses, consensus statements, and evidence from related autoimmune or cardiovascular populations were used to provide clinical and mechanistic context. Evidence was interpreted according to study design, population specificity, and recognised methodological limitations. SjD-specific observational evidence supports an association with systemic immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, subclinical vascular injury, and selected cardiopulmonary manifestations. Sex-hormone signalling, menopausal changes, and X-linked immune mechanisms may contribute to female susceptibility, although their relationship with CV outcomes remains largely hypothetical. Evidence concerning coronary microvascular dysfunction, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, arrhythmias, autonomic dysfunction, and pulmonary hypertension is heterogeneous and frequently derived from small cohorts or indirect evidence. In women, fatigue, dyspnoea, pain, palpitations, and autonomic symptoms may overlap with systemic manifestations of SjD and complicate recognition of concomitant CV disease. Cardiovascular care in women with SjD may benefit from combining established prevention and symptom-driven diagnostic pathways with attention to interstitial lung disease, systemic organ involvement, treatment exposure, and reproductive and hormonal history. The proposed assessment framework is intended to provide practical clinical orientation and to support individualised decision-making, rather than to define a standardised SjD-specific screening pathway. Prospective, sex-disaggregated studies are needed to clarify the prognostic relevance of these factors and to inform future recommendations regarding cardiovascular assessment and follow-up.

items.title: Responsiveness of patient-reported outcomes by disease trajectory in systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a heterogeneous autoimmune disease with persistent symptoms that profoundly impair quality of life yet are often under-recognized by clinician-assessed instruments. Patient-reported outcomes (PROs) are increasingly incorporated in clinical trials to capture treatment benefit from the patient perspective. However, the responsiveness of PRO instruments and their alignment with clinician-assessed disease activity across distinct SLE trajectories remain incompletely defined. We evaluated the longitudinal responsiveness and convergent validity of PRO measures across predefined disease trajectory classes. Secondary analysis of pooled patient-level data from two phase III randomized clinical trials of belimumab in adults with active SLE (n = 1908), stratified into four previously derived trajectory classes defined by baseline disease activity and treatment response. PROs included FACIT-Fatigue, SF-36 PCS and MCS, EQ-5D-3L, and EQ-VAS. Responsiveness was quantified using standardized response means (SRMs). Convergent validity was evaluated using repeated-measures correlations between within-person changes in PROs and clinician-assessed disease activity measures (SLEDAI-2K, BILAG, and PGA), with sensitivity analyses performed to assess the robustness of findings. FACIT-F and SF-36 PCS generally demonstrated the greatest responsiveness, while EQ-5D-3L showed smaller changes and less consistent responsiveness across classes and timepoints. FACIT-F demonstrated early responsiveness, whereas SF-36 PCS showed sustained responsiveness over later follow-up. PRO changes were most consistently associated with PGA. Sensitivity analyses showed broadly similar patterns. FACIT-F and SF-36 PCS demonstrated the greatest responsiveness and alignment with clinician-assessed disease activity. EQ-5D-3L showed less consistent responsiveness, suggesting domain-specific PROs may better capture treatment benefit in SLE trials and health technology assessments.

items.title: Effects of microtrauma on joint structural changes in the Curdlan-injected SKG mouse model of ankylosing spondylitis.
items.abstract: Although microtrauma is considered a potential environmental factor in the development of ankylosing spondylitis (AS), there is a lack of experimental research regarding its precise contribution to disease pathogenesis. To induce physiological microtrauma, the right ankles of SKG mice were immobilized for a week using surgical plaster and a pipette tip to stimulate compensatory mechanical overload in the contralateral limb. Following the removal of the immobilization, the mice were intraperitoneally injected with 3 mg of Curdlan. In this model, the non-immobilized left ankle served as the microtraumatized group, while the immobilized right ankle served as the internal control. Arthritis severity was clinically scored weekly for 5 weeks. At 6 weeks, ankle, hip, and sacroiliac (SI) joint changes were evaluated using histological and micro-CT analyses. The microtraumatized (left) ankles of Curdlan-injected SKG mice exhibited exacerbated arthritis severity, synovitis, and enthesitis compared with the control ankles. Micro-CT analysis revealed a significantly elevated inflamed bone volume in the microtraumatized ankles. Immunohistochemistry showed markedly higher expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6) in the synovium and enthesis of the microtraumatized ankles. Notably, distant pathological changes, including proteoglycan loss and joint space narrowing, were also observed in the left hip joints. Collectively, these findings indicate that compensatory microtrauma significantly exacerbates joint inflammation and pathological bone destruction in the Curdlan-injected SKG mouse model, highlighting mechanical stress as a critical aggravating factor in AS progression.

items.title: Tubuloreticular Inclusions in Kidney Tissues of Patients with Lupus Nephritis: An Ultrastructural Biomarker of Type I Interferon-Driven Disease Activity.
items.abstract: Tubuloreticular inclusions (TRIs) in kidney tissues associate with type I interferon (IFN-I) pathway activation, but their clinical and pathological significance in lupus nephritis (LN) remains incompletely defined. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 327 patients with biopsy-confirmed LN at the National Clinical Research Center for Kidney Diseases from January 2023 to December 2025. TRIs were identified in kidney tissues by transmission electron microscopy in both glomerular endothelial cells (GEC) and peritubular capillary (PTC) endothelial cells. For semi-quantitative assessment, 10 capillary loops per glomerulus and 10 peritubular capillaries per case were examined; in cases with more than one glomerulus, loops were randomly selected from each glomerulus and the maximum score across all glomeruli was recorded as the GEC-TRI grade. The final TRI grade for each case was defined as the higher of the GEC-TRI and PTC-TRI grades, classified as grade 0 (no TRIs), grade 1 (TRIs in 1 of 10 capillary profiles) or grade 2 (TRIs in ≥2 of 10 capillary profiles), with patients subsequently grouped as TRI-negative (grade 0) or TRI-positive (grade 1 or 2). Clinical, pathological, immunofluorescence and extrarenal manifestations were compared between groups. In a subset, peripheral blood RNA sequencing was performed to calculate IFN I scores and assess pathway activation. TRIs were observed in 207 of 327 patients (63.3%). Pathologically, TRI-positive patients exhibited lower chronicity index, higher frequency of segmental loop necrosis, along with reduced rates of vascular lesions, interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (all P < 0.05). On immunofluorescence, increased deposition of IgM and C1q and a higher prevalence of full-house pattern were observed in TRI-positive patients (all P < 0.05); C3 deposition showed a significant stepwise increase across TRI grades (P = 0.03), though the dichotomized comparison was not significant (P = 0.06). Clinically, they had higher SLE Disease Activity Index scores, increased urinary red blood cell counts and elevated proteinuria (all P < 0.05). They also demonstrated lower serum complement levels, increased immunoglobulin levels (e.g., IgA) and higher prevalence of multiple autoantibodies (e.g., anti-dsDNA; all P < 0.05). TRI-positive patients also showed heightened IFN-I signatures and higher prevalence of extrarenal manifestations, including mucocutaneous, musculoskeletal, hematological, pulmonary involvement, serositis and organic brain syndrome (all P < 0.05). TRIs are highly prevalent in kidney tissues of patients with LN. They identify a distinct IFN-I-driven disease subset, offering a practical histopathological marker of heightened activity and potential target for therapeutic stratification.

items.title: Effectiveness of Newly Initiated Tofacitinib and Biologic DMARDs in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: This new-user, active comparator study of patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) evaluated the real-world effectiveness of tofacitinib versus biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs) using data from the US OM1 PremiOM™ RA dataset. This analysis included patients with RA aged ≥ 18 years initiating tofacitinib or bDMARDs (tumor necrosis factor inhibitors, TNFi; abatacept; interleukin-6 inhibitors, IL-6i) from January 1, 2013-March 13, 2024, with > 1 Clinical Disease Activity Index (CDAI) score in the 45 days prior to and including the index date. Propensity score weighting adjusted for differences in baseline characteristics between treatment groups. Crude incidence rates were calculated to estimate the first record of CDAI remission (CDAI ≤ 2.8) and low disease activity (LDA; CDAI ≤ 10.0) at 6 and 12 months. Cox regression was used to estimate weighted hazard ratios. Subgroup analyses assessed heterogeneity of treatment effects (HTE). The final sample size across cohorts was 3681 (tofacitinib), 11,667 (TNFi), 3528 (abatacept), and 2464 (IL-6i). At baseline, the proportion of patients with observed RA disease duration ≥ 2 years was 48.7-70.0% across cohorts; use of 2/3/≥ 4 prior biologic/targeted synthetic (b/ts) DMARDs was 21.4%/10.2%/5.0% (tofacitinib), versus 8.1%/3.0%/2.4% (TNFi), 19.2%/8.3%/3.7% (abatacept), and 25.4%/13.7%/10.5% (IL-6i). In the overall and TNFi-experienced population, there were no statistically significant differences in CDAI remission and LDA rates between treatments at 6 and 12 months. Potential HTE was observed among subgroups of age ≥ 50 years, obesity, prior b/tsDMARD use, corticosteroid use, and Sjӧgren's disease. At 6 and 12 months, there were no significant differences in achieving or maintaining CDAI remission and LDA for tofacitinib versus TNFi, abatacept, and IL-6i among the overall and TNFi-experienced RA population in US clinical practice. Subgroup analyses suggest some potential HTE; however, interpretation is limited by the small number of outcome events. NCT06418529.

items.title: Clinical characteristics of headache in the patients with Neuro-Behçet's disease.
items.abstract: Behçet's disease (BD) is a chronic vascular-inflammatory condition of unknown pathogenesis presenting with mucocutaneous lesions, attacks of uveitis that may lead to blindness, and involvement of many systems including vascular, musculo-skeletal system and the gastrointestinal tract. The objective of this study was to examine the frequency of various forms of headache in patients diagnosed with BD, the characteristics of headache in BD, the characteristics of attacks, and the relationship between the disease and headache attacks. A total of 35 patients with Neuro-Behçet's disease (NBD) aged ≥ 18 years, who were followed at the Department of Neurology of XX University between 2021 and 2026, were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were evaluated for demographic characteristics, headache characteristics and severity, imaging studies, cerebrospinal fluid findings, relationship to attacks, and acute and chronic treatment. The most common complaint was headache. It was observed that headache could be of primary type as migraine or tension-type headache or secondary headache due to neurological involvement. Headache in NBD was frequently observed during BD attacks (aphthosis and/or uveitis) or in temporal proximity to these attacks, suggesting a possible association with disease activity. Headache in NBD is heterogeneous and cannot be fully explained by primary headache syndromes alone; a substantial proportion is associated with disease activity and neurological involvement. The temporal association observed between headache and disease attacks may indicate an association between headache and disease activity. Therefore, in patients presenting with headache, NBD involvement should also be considered.

items.title: Frailty and Rheumatoid Arthritis: Key Insights and the Road Ahead.
items.abstract: People with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) experience premature aging and RA is associated with poor health outcomes. Frailty tools offer a holistic view of an individual's health status that may inform treatment strategies in RA. This review provides an overview of frailty in RA including methods of measurement, associations with clinical outcomes, and potential paths for frailty intervention. Frailty is common in RA, affecting approximately one-third of patients, with prevalence estimates varying according to the measurement instrument used. The causes of frailty are not well studied but likely include a combination of chronic systemic inflammation, immunosenescence, deconditioning and medication effects. Frailty is consistently associated with higher disease activity, poorer physical function, depression, pain, reduced quality of life, and greater comorbidity burden. Longitudinal studies show that frailty predicts hospitalization, serious infections, osteoporotic fractures, functional decline, readmission, and mortality, independent of traditional clinical risk factors and comorbidity indices. Emerging evidence also supports a bidirectional relationship between frailty and RA disease activity, suggesting that some aspects of frailty may be modifiable through improved disease control. Frailty-specific interventions have not yet been studied in RA, however, RA disease control, medication optimization and promotion of physical activity are likely to improve frailty in this high-risk population. Frailty is an important predictor of poor health outcomes in RA and may be amenable to interventions. Incorporation of frailty assessment into clinical care and clinical trials will be essential to move the field forward.

items.title: IgG4-related disease of the pelvic floor musculature mimicking neoplasm: a case report with imaging-pathologic correlation.
items.abstract: IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is an immune-mediated fibroinflammatory condition that can form tumefactive mass-like lesions and mimic malignancy across organ systems. We describe a rare presentation involving the deep pelvic floor musculature with imaging-pathologic correlation while underscoring diagnostic pitfalls. A 49-year-old man with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus, night sweats, and left lower quadrant abdominal pain underwent CT of the abdomen and pelvis, which demonstrated a right posterior pelvic sidewall mass and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. Pelvic MRI demonstrated an ill-defined intramuscular mass centered in the right iliococcygeus and pubococcygeus muscles. Relative to skeletal muscle, the lesion demonstrated iso- to low T1 signal intensity, intermediate T2 signal intensity, restricted diffusion, and moderate, diffuse contrast enhancement, raising concern for neoplasm or an inflammatory process. Image-guided biopsy revealed fibrotic soft tissue with severe lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate and increased IgG4-reactive plasma cells. The IgG4+/IgG+ plasma cell ratio was > 75%, consistent with IgG4-RD when integrated with the clinical, laboratory, imaging and pathologic findings. IgG4-related disease with mass-like involvement of the pelvic floor musculature has not, to the best of our knowledge, been previously reported in the English literature. This entity can present as an ill-defined, enhancing, diffusion-restricting intramuscular mass and therefore may mimic a neoplastic process.

items.title: Identification of a systemic lupus erythematosus disease signature in resting naive B cells.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune condition with alternating phases of heightened symptoms and periods of disease inactivity. Our investigation focuses on the distinct molecular profiles of resting naive B cells from both active and inactive SLE states in female adults, primarily of Black ancestry. We identified a distinct transcriptome and epigenome during inactive SLE. Transcriptional patterns indicated an increase in distinct cytokine signaling pathway expression in SLE B cells, encompassing both common and disease activity-specific components. Specifically, while both disease states exhibited interferon signatures, increased expression of IL-12, TNF-α/NF-κB, and CD40 signaling pathway genes was enriched in inactive disease. While some regions exhibited comparable epigenetic features in both disease states, such as TLR7 signaling genes, others were distinct. Chromatin accessibility in inactive disease indicated the involvement of MEF2 and bHLH family factors, such as E2A/E2-2, while active disease regions were defined by IRF family factors. This study illuminates both disease-associated programs and molecular changes to cell activation pathways capable of directing B cells toward diverse effector fates in active or inactive SLE. Our data also offer insights of particular importance for the design and monitoring of B cell-targeting treatments.

items.title: Initial treatment strategies and outcomes across haemodynamic thresholds and risk stratification in incident systemic sclerosis-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension: a EUSTAR analysis.
items.abstract: Real-world initial treatment strategies in SSc-PAH remain incompletely described. We aimed to characterise these strategies across haemodynamic thresholds and risk strata and evaluate outcome associations. We analysed treatment-naïve SSc-PAH patients in EUSTAR (2000-2021) fulfilling the 2022 haemodynamic definition. Initial therapy comprised treatment initiated within 4 months of RHC. As-treated (AT) analyses were primary and intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses supportive. Outcomes were all-cause mortality and 36-month PAH progression. Among 301 patients, 198 (66%) initiated therapy and 170 maintained therapy for ≥3 months. Therapy was initiated in 31% with milder haemodynamic impairment (mPAP 21-24 mmHg and/or PVR 2-3 WU) versus 79% fulfilling the previous haemodynamic definition; combination therapy increased from 14% to 67% across low- to high-risk strata. Over a median 3.9 years, 125 (42%) died and 85/227 (37%) progressed. Adjusted ITT analyses showed no association with either outcome, whereas adjusted AT analyses showed lower mortality risk with sustained monotherapy and combination therapy (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.27-0.92 and HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.18-0.88, respectively) and lower PAH progression risk with sustained initial therapy (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.18-0.76). In the milder haemodynamic subgroup, the mortality estimate was directionally consistent but imprecise. Initial treatment strategies reflected haemodynamic severity and baseline risk, while variation suggested potential implementation gaps. Sustained initial therapy was associated with lower risks of mortality and PAH progression. Contrasting ITT and AT estimates highlight challenges in observational treatment-outcome comparisons. Findings in the milder haemodynamic subgroup support dedicated prospective studies.

items.title: Central sensitization in rheumatoid arthritis: a cross-sectional analysis of functional disability, disease activity, and glucocorticoid use.
items.abstract: To examine the clinical correlates of central sensitization (CS) in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and to perform an exploratory analysis of its association with glucocorticoid use. This single-center, cross-sectional study included 286 patients with RA (≥18 years) fulfilling the 2010 EULAR/ACR classification criteria and receiving stable treatment for at least 3 months. Demographic data, clinical characteristics, and treatment history were recorded. Participants completed the Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI) and the Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQ). Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with CS. CS was present in 31.5% ( n  = 90) of patients. Patients with CS exhibited significantly higher tender joint counts and DAS28-CRP scores, while CRP levels and swollen joint counts were comparable between groups. In univariable analyses, CS was associated with younger age, female sex, longer disease duration, greater biologic exposure, and more frequent current steroid use (54.4% vs. 34.7%, p  = 0.002). Multivariable logistic regression revealed that higher HAQ scores remained the sole independent factor associated with CS (OR: 5.32, p  < 0.001), whereas the initial association with corticosteroid use lost significance after adjustment. CS in RA is independently linked to functional disability rather than objective inflammation, highlighting a potential discordance between clinical findings and symptom burden. Recognition of these non-inflammatory mechanisms may help prevent unnecessary treatment escalation, particularly glucocorticoid overuse, and support more appropriate pain management strategies.

items.title: Metabolic-Epigenetic Reprogramming of Fibroblast-Like Synoviocytes in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Perspectives for Traditional Chinese Medicine.
items.abstract: In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), persistent synovial inflammation and clinical relapse cannot be fully explained by immune activation alone, as fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) can acquire stable pathogenic states that sustain synovitis and joint destruction. Metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic remodeling are functionally integrated in RA-FLS, thereby promoting hyperproliferation, invasiveness, apoptosis resistance, and inflammatory memory. In this review, we summarize the interplay between altered cellular metabolism and epigeneticmechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, non-coding RNAs, RNA modifications, and chromatin remodeling, and discuss how this interplay contributes tostabilizing pathogenic FLS phenotypes.We further discuss gut microbiota-associated metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, tryptophan derivatives, and one-carbon metabolites, as potential mediators linking systemic metabolic imbalance to FLS epigenetic states. These metabolites may act through histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibition, modulation of methyl donor availability, and receptor-mediated inflammatory signaling. From the perspective of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), we propose that TCM formulations and bioactive compounds may modulate this network through microbiota-dependent metabolic remodeling and direct suppression of FLS activation. Finally, we identify current evidence gaps and highlight emerging therapeutic strategies, including metabolomics-guided fecal microbiota transplantation and FLS-targeted epigenetic interventions. This review highlights metabolic-epigenetic reprogramming as a key mechanism underlying persistent RA-FLS phenotypes. Interactions among thegut microbiota, microbial metabolites, and epigenetic regulation provide a promising framework for linking systemic metabolic disturbances to local joint damage. Future studies integrating multi-omics profiling, microbiome modulation, and FLS-targeted epigenetic interventions are needed to clarify causality and facilitate more precise therapeutic strategies.

items.title: African recommendations for diagnosis and management of systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA) - a PAFLAR initiative.
items.abstract: To develop evidence-based recommendations for diagnosis and treatment of children and adolescents with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA), taking into consideration the socioeconomic status and availability of medications in African countries. A steering group composed of five PAFLAR members formulated questions in PICO format (Patient/Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome), conducted a systematic literature review, and identified experts in pediatric rheumatology throughout Africa. The Delphi method was used to reach consensus among the experts on the recommendations for diagnosis and treatment of sJIA patients. The online Delphi questionnaire was sent to the 22 experts selected by the steering committee, who were asked to vote for each statement and to provide their suggestions for modifications or rewording. A 100% response rate was obtained. A minimum agreement of 70% among the voting panel was required. A total of 15 recommendations were formulated, 4 regarding diagnosis and 11 regarding treatment. The percentage of agreement with the recommendations ranged from 72.7% to 95%. We present the first African recommendations for diagnosis and management of sJIA. The feedback about the application of these recommendations in pediatric rheumatology centers will serve as the basis for future revisions in the light of African-specific experiences and insights.

items.title: A Review of Detection Probes for Vanin-1: Development and Biological Applications in Various Inflammatory Diseases.
items.abstract: Vascular non-inflammatory molecule-1 (Vanin-1), also known as pantetheinase, is a key enzyme that regulates oxidative stress, inflammatory responses, and metabolic processes by catalyzing the hydrolysis of pantetheine into cysteamine and pantothenic acid. Recent studies have progressively elucidated its pivotal role in various pathological processes, including acute kidney injury (AKI), inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), liver injury, and rheumatoid arthritis (RA). As an important biomarker for early diagnosis and assessment of treatment efficacy, it has attracted widespread attention and driven the rapid development of highly sensitive and specific detection tools. This article provides a systematic review of Vanin-1 probes developed in recent years, covering fluorescent, chemiluminescent, bioluminescent, and electrochemical sensors, with a focus on their molecular design principles, detection mechanisms, performance characteristics, and biological applications. In addition, this article outlines future trends in Vanin-1 probe technologies, providing a comprehensive theoretical and methodological reference to support further basic research and clinical translation applications related to Vanin-1.

items.title: Cutaneous efficacy and glucocorticoid-sparing effects of anifrolumab in systemic lupus erythematosus: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.abstract: To evaluate the cutaneous efficacy and glucocorticoid-sparing effects of anifrolumab in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and to assess composite disease activity and flare-related and safety outcomes. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through 20 April 2026. Meta-analyses were restricted to randomized controlled trials comparing intravenous anifrolumab 300 mg every 4 weeks plus standard therapy with placebo plus standard therapy; TULIP-SC and overlapping reports were synthesized narratively. Risk ratios (RRs) or rate ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models in the primary analyses, with fixed-effect models applied in sensitivity analyses. Modified Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ) sensitivity analyses were performed for outcomes with substantial heterogeneity and a small number of contributing studies. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using RoB 2 and GRADE, respectively. In all, 12 reports from five independent trials were included; four intravenous trials contributed up to 1,203 participants. The Week 52 CLASI-A50 estimate was based on two trials (n = 165), not the full 1,203-participant IV evidence set. Random-effects pooling showed that anifrolumab improved Week 52 CLASI-A50 response based on two trials among patients with baseline CLASI-A ≥ 10 (RR 1.52, 95% CI 1.04 to 2.24), sustained oral glucocorticoid reduction in those receiving ≥ 10 mg/day at baseline (RR 1.56, 95% CI 1.30 to 1.87), and BICLA response (RR 1.66, 95% CI 1.41 to 1.94). SRI-4 (RR 1.39, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.87; I² = 80.8%), LLDAS attainment (RR 1.80, 95% CI 1.19 to 2.73; I² = 57.2%), and annualized flare rate (rate ratio 0.65, 95% CI 0.47 to 0.91; I² = 56.5%) favored anifrolumab but were affected by heterogeneity or limited trial numbers. The incidence of any adverse events was slightly higher (RR 1.09, 95% CI 1.03 to 1.16), whereas serious adverse events and discontinuations due to adverse events did not differ significantly. Supplementary analyses of selected adverse events of clinical interest suggested an increased risk of herpes zoster (RR 3.88, 95% CI 1.70 to 8.89), although event numbers were limited and these analyses were supplementary. Modified HKSJ sensitivity analyses yielded wider intervals crossing the null for SRI-4, LLDAS, annualized flare rate, serious adverse events, and adverse events leading to discontinuation. Intravenous anifrolumab improved Week 52 CLASI-A50 response in the two contributing trials of patients with baseline CLASI-A ≥ 10 and facilitated sustained glucocorticoid reduction in the prespecified glucocorticoid subgroup. DerSimonian-Laird point estimates for secondary efficacy outcomes generally favored anifrolumab, but the HKSJ sensitivity analyses for heterogeneous outcomes and the limited safety data warrant cautious interpretation. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261367219.

items.title: Dynamic changes in CBC-derived inflammatory indices before and during acute coronary syndrome in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a within-patient paired study.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with excess cardiovascular risk, but within-patient changes in complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices at the onset of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) are not well described. We compared pre-event and acute-phase values in the same patients and contextualized pre-event values against a healthy cohort. This retrospective, single-center, within-patient paired study reviewed hospital records from July 1, 2018, to December 30, 2025 (approximately 90 months). Among 3,960 hospitalized patients with RA, 89 had clinician-confirmed ACS and qualifying paired CBC measurements. Acute-phase CBCs were obtained within 24 hours after symptom onset, and pre-event CBCs were the most recent routine measurements obtained more than 14 days before the event. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) were calculated and natural log-transformed. Pre-event values were also compared with a healthy cohort (n = 110), with age- and sex-adjusted analyses used because residual demographic imbalance was present. Pre-event log(NLR), log(SII), and log(SIRI) were higher in the RA cohort than in healthy controls and remained higher after adjustment for age and sex (all P< 0.001). Within-patient analyses showed increases during ACS, with mean Δlog values of 0.466 for NLR, 0.508 for SII, and 0.381 for SIRI (all Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted q< 0.001). Neutrophilia increased from 11.2% before the event to 41.6% during ACS (McNemar P< 0.001). Exploratory subgroup estimates were heterogeneous and non-monotonic across several small strata; changes did not differ materially between remission/low and moderate/high RA activity groups. Among patients with RA who developed ACS, CBC-derived inflammatory indices were higher than in a healthy comparison cohort before the event and increased further within the first 24 hours of ACS. The paired design quantifies change relative to each patient's own pre-event value. Without a non-RA ACS comparator, however, the study cannot establish RA-specific inflammatory priming or a causal chronic-to-acute mechanism. Prospective studies with serial sampling and clinical outcomes are needed.

items.title: Case Report: Value of MR relaxometry and spectroscopy in multimodal imaging characterization of limbic encephalitis in systemic sclerosis.
items.abstract: Central nervous system involvement is uncommon in systemic sclerosis, and inflammatory temporomesial syndromes in this context are rarely reported. We present a 58-year-old man with systemic sclerosis who developed subacute cognitive impairment and dialeptic seizures arising from the right temporal lobe. Video electroencephalography confirmed a right temporal seizure onset zone. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated enlargement and subtle T2 hyperintensity of the right hippocampus and amygdala, while fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography/computed tomography images showed focal hypermetabolism of the enlarged right amygdala. Proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy demonstrated bilateral reduction of total N-acetylaspartate compared with an age-matched healthy reference subject, with a more pronounced difference on the right, a pattern compatible with bilateral, right-accentuated neuronal dysfunction or injury. MR relaxometry demonstrated significant bilateral T2 prolongation in the amygdalae and hippocampal heads, whereas T1 abnormalities were more region-dependent, involving the right amygdala and both hippocampal heads. Serum testing detected anti-pyruvate dehydrogenase antibodies, whereas routine clinical neural antibody testing was negative. The patient became seizure-free under antiseizure medication and immunosuppressive therapy with cyclophosphamide. Notably, although the unilateral conventional imaging findings did not meet the bilateral mesial temporal criterion required by current consensus criteria for definite autoimmune limbic encephalitis, MR relaxometry revealed bilateral temporomesial abnormalities. This finding is consistent with available neuropathological and experimental evidence and suggests that routine imaging may underestimate disease extent. This case highlights a rare presentation of antibody-atypical limbic encephalitis in the setting of systemic sclerosis and illustrates how multimodal imaging can support diagnosis and tissue characterization when routine antibody testing is unrevealing.

items.title: Cardiovascular and mortality outcomes with JAK versus TNF inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis: a target trial emulation (CARDINAL-RA).
items.abstract: This study aims to compare cardiovascular and mortality outcomes of Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) versus tumor necrosis factor inhibitors (TNFi) in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) at elevated cardiovascular risk using target trial emulation. Within TriNetX, adults with RA aged ≥50 years and ≥1 cardiovascular risk factor initiating JAKi or TNFi were compared in a new-user, active-comparator design. Improved 1:1 propensity score matching incorporated demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, comorbidities, individual conventional synthetic DMARDs, oral corticosteroids, prior non-TNF biologic exposure, and baseline inflammatory markers. The primary outcome was MACE (nonfatal myocardial infarction or nonfatal ischemic stroke); the secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, and venous thromboembolism (VTE), with cataract as a prespecified negative control. Follow-up began 90 days after initiation. Cox models estimated hazard ratios, with 5-year Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidences and absolute risk differences per 1,000. Cohorts were separately matched by agent, sex, cardiovascular-risk stratum, and index era; E-values quantified sensitivity to unmeasured confounding. In 18,757 matched pairs, JAKi was not associated with excess MACE (HR 1.002, 0.923-1.088; +2.11 per 1,000). All-cause mortality, a secondary outcome, was higher with JAKi (HR 1.158, 1.058-1.268; p  = 0.0014; +10.4 per 1,000; E-value 1.586), whereas heart failure hospitalization (HR 1.019, 0.955-1.088) and VTE (HR 1.054, 0.961-1.156) did not differ; the negative control showed no excess (HR 0.934, 0.867-1.007). No agent showed a significant excess in MACE or mortality (mortality HR 1.052 tofacitinib, 1.213 baricitinib, and 1.090 upadacitinib); the only nominally significant agent-level finding was VTE with baricitinib (HR 1.364, 1.028-1.809; 198 events). A three-component composite including death was non-significant (HR 1.058, 0.992-1.127). No consistent effect modification was seen by sex, cardiovascular risk burden, or index year. JAKi initiation was not associated with excess MACE (primary outcome), heart failure hospitalization, or VTE. A modest excess in all-cause mortality was observed as a secondary outcome, with no signal for any individual agent. This association was of modest robustness (E-value 1.586) and was not reproduced in any agent-specific cohort, so residual channeling bias cannot be excluded. The null MACE result should not be read as class-wide cardiovascular safety reassurance nor the mortality signal as an established causal effect.

items.title: Radiomics-Based prediction of renal prognosis in ANCA-associated vasculitis.
items.abstract: To develop and validate a non-invasive prediction model combining renal CT radiomics features and clinical markers for assessing long-term renal prognosis at 1, 3, and 5 years in patients with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV). A retrospective cohort of 262 AAV patients from Peking Union Medical College Hospital (2015-2020) was analyzed. Radiomics features (morphological, first-order, and texture) were extracted from segmented renal parenchyma on abdominopelvic CT. Clinical markers included demographics, serum creatinine, complement component 3 (C3), and other laboratory indicators. Renal volume, serum creatinine, and complement component 3 (C3) were pre-specified as predictors based on a priori biological rationale, and XGBoost was employed for model construction. Performance was evaluated via ROC-AUC (receiver operating characteristic/area under the curve), F1 score, decision curve analysis, and calibration curves. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis assessed feature contributions, and Kaplan-Meier curves with Bonferroni-corrected log-rank tests were used for survival stratification. The mean follow-up was 40.8 months; 59 patients (23%) developed ESRD (56 within 3 years) and 29 (11%) died. The combined model (renal volume + sCr + C3) achieved an AUC of 0.93 for 3-year ESRD prediction (clinical-only model: 0.91), with renal volume independently associated with ESRD (Wald p  = 0.004). For the 3-year composite outcome, the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.84 (clinical-only: 0.81) with significantly improved reclassification (IDI p  = 0.018; category-free NRI p  = 0.024). In pre-specified median-based Kaplan-Meier analyses, reduced renal volume (≤ 130.6 mL), elevated serum creatinine (> 177.5 μmol/L) and lower C3 (≤ 0.97 g/L) were associated with poorer 3-year ESRD-free survival (log-rank p  ≤ 0.002). The integrated radiomics-clinical model provides accurate, non-invasive risk stratification for long-term renal outcomes in AAV, facilitating personalized treatment.

items.title: Malignant erythema as a high-specificity cutaneous indicator of malignancy in adult dermatomyositis: a retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Dermatomyositis (DM) is associated with a substantially elevated risk of malignancy, yet the cutaneous features predictive of cancer risk in adults remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to characterize cutaneous manifestations and clinical factors associated with malignancy in adult DM, with a focus on malignant erythema. This retrospective cohort study included 261 adults with DM admitted between 2016 and 2023 and followed up till June 2025. Clinical data, laboratory indicators (including creatine kinase [CK] and lactate dehydrogenase [LDH]), autoantibodies, and skin findings were systematically evaluated. The primary outcome was the occurrence of malignant tumors. Twenty‑six patients (10%) developed malignancy. Malignant erythema was identified in 35 patients (13.3%), among whom 14 (40%) had malignancy. Both anti-transcription intermediary factor-1 γ (anti-TIF-1 γ) antibodies and malignant erythema were independently associated with malignancy (odds ratio [OR] = 18.231, 95% confidence interval [CI] 4.568-72.756, P < 0.001; OR = 17.588, 95% CI 2.151-143.824, P = 0.007). Malignant erythema demonstrated higher specificity for tumor prediction than anti-TIF-1 γ antibodies (91.1% vs. 86%, P < 0.001), while sensitivity did not differ significantly (53.8% vs. 73.1%, P = 0.190). while. Malignant erythema is a distinctive poikilodermatous manifestation strongly associated with malignancy in adult DM. Its high specificity suggests that malignant erythema may serve as a valuable clinical indicator for malignancy risk and a useful complement to anti-TIF-1 γ antibody testing.
