items.title: Multifactorial explanatory model of self-reported sleep disturbance in people with rheumatoid arthritis: a structural equation approach.
items.abstract: Sleep disturbance is a common and disabling symptom among patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). This study aimed to test a multifactorial explanatory model of cross-sectional associations among factors related to self-reported sleep disturbance in RA. This was an ancillary analysis of an observational, cross-sectional, single-centre study including patients with RA. Sleep disturbance, disease activity, perceived disease impact, depressive and anxiety symptoms, and personality traits were assessed using validated questionnaires. Structural equation modelling (SEM) was used to examine the associations between sleep disturbance and the remaining variables. A total of 313 patients (82% female; mean age 60±12 years; disease duration 12±9 years) were included. The final model showed an acceptable fit to the data [χ2(71)=178.04, χ2/df=2.50, p<0.005; CFI=0.95; GFI=0.92; TLI=0.94; RMSEA=0.07, p=0.004, 95% CI=0.06 to 0.08] and explained 57% of the variance of self-reported sleep disturbance (R2=0.57). Disease activity was positively associated with disease impact (β=0.23; p<0.001), which was significantly associated with sleep disturbance (β=0.65; p=0.001). 'Positive' personality traits were inversely associated with self-reported sleep disturbance (β= -0.51; p=0.001), with direct (β= -0.16; p=0.006) and indirect associations (β= -0.35; p=0.001) through perceived disease impact. They were also inversely associated with depression (β= -0.77; p=0.001) and anxiety (β= -0.80; p<0.001). Depression and anxiety were positively associated with perceived disease impact (β=0.38; p=0.001 and β=0.30; p<0.001, respectively). 'Positive' personality traits and perceived disease impact appear to be significantly associated with self-reported sleep disturbance in RA patients, while disease activity, depression, and anxiety showed comparatively smaller associations within the model. These findings support the need for a holistic, multidisciplinary approach to RA management.

items.title: Factors associated with chronic kidney disease in patients with gout: a two-centre study incorporating ultrasonographic features.
items.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a significant comorbidity in patients with gout, yet the specific phenotypes associated with its prevalence remain insufficiently characterised. This study aimed to evaluate the association between clinical indicators and ultrasonographic features with CKD using a transparent, interpretable machine learning approach. This cross-sectional bicentric study analysed a cohort of 666 patients with gout, who were partitioned into a derivation cohort (n=500) for model development and internal validation, and an independent validation cohort (n=166). Three architectures (GLM, Random Forest, SVM) modelled associations between biomarkers and CKD status. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis quantified individual variable contributions, and a dynamic nomogram visualised cumulative relevance. Six key correlates were identified, comprising two clinical indicators (age and hypertension) and four ultrasonographic findings (bone erosion, high-burden (≥3 joints) tophi, synovial hyperplasia, and double contour sign). The GLM demonstrated the strongest associative performance, with an AUC of 0.842 (internal) and 0.835 (independent cohort), indicating high discriminative power. SHAP analysis identified advanced age and ultrasound-detected tophi as the most influential contributors to the observed associations. DCA and calibration plots confirmed that the framework accurately reflected the underlying probability distribution. We established an interpretable analytical framework that characterises the clinical and ultrasonographic profile associated with CKD in gout. By integrating imaging markers with clinical indicators, this approach identifies associated phenotypes, providing a transparent reference for individualised assessment and enhanced clinical vigilance regarding renal status.

items.title: Prokineticin 2 promotes endoplasmic reticulum stress in rheumatoid arthritis by potentiating IL-1β-induced inflammation.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterised by persistent synovial inflammation and progressive joint destruction. Although current therapies have greatly improved disease management, many patients show an inadequate response or develop resistance to existing therapies. Therefore, identifying novel molecular targets remains essential to improve therapeutic outcomes, particularly in refractory cases. Commercially available rheumatoid arthritis-derived fibroblast-like synoviocytes (RA-FLS) were stimulated with pro-inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and tumour necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), to evaluate cytokine-induced gene expression changes. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and functional assays were used to explore signalling pathways regulated by the candidate gene prokineticin 2 (PK2). Expression of pathway-related markers was validated by qRT-PCR and Western blotting. The in vivo role of PK2 was further assessed in a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mouse model. PK2 expression was significantly increased in synovial tissue from RA patients. In vitro, IL-1β and TNF-α upregulated PK2 expression in RA-FLS. Transcriptomic analysis showed that co-stimulation with PK2 and IL-1β significantly enriched pathways involved in protein processing in the endoplasmic reticulum. Further experiments demonstrated that combined PK2 and IL-1β stimulation increased the expression of XBP1, GRP78, CHOP, and HSPA6. In vivo, PK2 aggravated joint inflammation and tissue damage in CIA mice, whereas the PK2 antagonist PKRA7 significantly alleviated disease severity. PK2 is a key RA-associated gene that is closely involved in endoplasmic reticulum protein-processing pathways. Targeting PK2-mediated ER stress may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for RA.

items.title: Utility of follow-up cardiac magnetic resonance imaging in patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
items.abstract: Cardiac involvement in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) occurs in approximately 20-40% of patients and has been shown to be a major predictor of mortality. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) can detect late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), which can indicate myocardial inflammation and/or fibrosis. However, the role of CMRI at diagnosis and to monitor evolution of cardiac manifestations in EGPA remains unclear. Our aim was to describe the CMRI findings in our EGPA patient cohort, including the presence and persistence of LGE, and to report on the clinical outcomes observed during follow-up. This monocentric retrospective descriptive cohort study included 75 patients diagnosed with EGPA, who were seen at least twice between 2015 and January 2023. Among these 75 patients (male 56%, mean age at diagnosis 45 years), 30 patients underwent CMRI at diagnosis, 9 (30%) of whom had cardiac symptoms. All 30 patients (100%) were treated with glucocorticoids, with 13 (43%) also receiving cyclophosphamide. 16/30 (53%) had LGE on first CMRI; 10/11 had persistent LGE on second CMRI, 4/4 had LGE on third CMRI, and 2/2 had LGE on fourth CMRI. Of these 30 patients, 3 (10%) had cardiovascular events at follow-up, 2 of whom had atrial fibrillation (neither had LGE on their CMRIs), and 1 of whom had coronary artery disease requiring stenting (with LGE on his 4 CMRIs). The role of CMRIs to study and monitor cardiac involvement in EGPA remains unclear. LGE most often persists despite treatment, with no apparent association with adverse cardiac outcomes in this cohort.

items.title: Incorporation of patient-reported outcomes in the clinical risk score to improve relapse prediction in ANCA-associated vasculitis.
items.abstract: To evaluate whether integration of patient-reported outcomes (PROs), particularly the 36-item short form health survey (SF-36), with the French Vasculitis Study Group relapse score (FRS) improves relapse prediction in patients with microscopic polyangiitis (MPA) or granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA). This retrospective cohort study included 98 patients with MPA or GPA whose baseline and first-year follow-up SF-36 data were available. The predictive accuracy of the FRS, baseline SF-36 physical component summary (PCS) and mental component summary (MCS), and first-year cumulative SF-36 PCS and MCS for relapse was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. The area under the curve (AUC) with 95% confidence interval (CI) was estimated for each variable. A combination of FRS and PRO with higher accuracy was developed using multivariable Cox regression incorporating variables significantly associated with relapse. During a median follow-up of 50.9 months, 28 patients (28.6%) experienced relapse. The FRS (AUC=0.666, 95% CI=0.552-0.780, p=0.010) and first-year cumulative SF-36 PCS (AUC=0.629, 95% CI=0.503-0.755, p=0.047) significantly predicted relapse, whereas baseline SF-36 PCS and MCS and first-year cumulative SF-36 MCS did not. A combination of the FRS and first-year cumulative SF-36 PCS demonstrated improved predictive performance (AUC=0.727, 95% CI=0.623-0.830, p<0.001). The first-year cumulative SF-36 PCS was independently associated with relapse in patients with MPA or GPA, and its integration with the FRS improved relapse risk prediction. These findings support a multidimensional approach incorporating both clinical and patient-reported data to better stratify relapse risk and inform treatment planning in MPA or GPA.

items.title: Senescent-like activated naive B cells contribute to progression to clinical rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease marked by joint and systemic inflammation. Anticitrullinated protein antibodies identify an at-risk stage that precedes clinical RA, yet the mechanisms driving disease progression remain poorly understood. Here we show that anticitrullinated-protein-antibody-positive individuals who progressed to RA exhibited a marked expansion of CXCR5 + CD69 + -activated naive B cells (aNAVs) before disease onset. These cells displayed inflammatory and senescent-like transcriptional programs and expressed polyreactive, autoreactive IgM B cell receptors. The expansion, activation and senescent-like phenotype of aNAVs were validated in multiple independent preclinical RA cohorts, and aNAVs were detectable in RA synovium. In vitro, aNAVs stimulated with citrullinated antigens promoted T cell activation in a human-leukocyte-antigen-dependent manner. Chronic exposure to citrullinated antigens and CpG (an innate immune stimulant) synergistically drove activation and senescent-like programming in naive B cells from individuals with RA. These findings identify senescent-like aNAVs as potential contributors and therapeutic targets for RA prevention.

items.title: FMO2+ fibroblasts as a potential disease-associated subset in the submandibular gland of IgG4-related disease: insights from single-cell RNA sequencing comparative analysis with the labial gland in primary Sjögren's syndrome.
items.abstract: To perform a comprehensive analysis of the immune landscapes in submandibular glands of IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) and labial salivary glands of primary Sjögren's syndrome (pSS). Five single-cell transcriptomics datasets of submandibular glands (SG) harvested from IgG4-RD patients and seven single-cell transcriptomics datasets of labial glands (LG) derived from pSS patients were processed and integrated by Seurat and Harmony R packages. After identifying cell types by classic marker genes, differential abundance analysis, functional enrichment and cell-cell communication were performed. After integrating single-cell RNA sequencing datasets, thirteen distinct subsets were identified. Differential abundance analysis revealed significant enrichment of LZ_GC B cells, DZ_GC B cells, Naive B cells, IgG4+plasma cells, CD4+DUSP4+MAF+T, CD4+TCM, CD8+TEM, Tfh, Treg, FMO2+ monocytes, M2 macrophages and FMO2+ fibroblasts in SG from patients with IgG4-RD compared to those in LG tissues in patients with pSS. FMO2+ fibroblasts were heterogeneous from other subpopulations with high expression of SELENOP, SEPTIN7, SELENOW, CCN1, LHFPL6, BEX3, CCN2, REX1BD, TMEM35B, TLE5. Gene Ontology (GO) analysis of the differentially expressed genes implicated this population in critical processes, including the humoral immune response, oxidative phosphorylation, and fibroblast proliferation. Moreover, we found the chemerin signalling pathway was the primary ligand-receptor interaction between fibroblasts and macrophages in SG from IgG4-RD. Specifically, Chemerin (encoded by RARRES2), the ligand in the CHEMERIN signalling pathway, was mainly expressed in fibroblasts and its receptors CMKLR1 and CCRL2 were primarily expressed on both macrophages and fibroblasts. FMO2+ fibroblasts emerged as a candidate cell subset potentially associated with the submandibular gland micro-environment in IgG4-RD. These findings provided a foundation for future functional studies to elucidate the potential roles of fibroblast-immune cell interactions in the pathogenesis of IgG4-RD.

items.title: Comparative assessment of the C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio, platelet-to-albumin ratio, and prognostic nutritional index in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease that requires regular disease activity assessment to guide treatment and improve outcomes. Composite inflammatory and nutritional biomarkers are promising adjunctive tools for monitoring disease activity. This comparative study aimed to evaluate the levels of C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR), platelet-to-albumin ratio (PAR), and prognostic nutritional index (PNI) in RA patients and healthy controls, and to compare their diagnostic performance and utility for disease activity assessment. The study included 165 RA patients and 167 age- and sex-matched controls. Disease activity of RA was assessed using the Disease Activity Score-28 based on erythrocyte sedimentation rate (DAS28-ESR) and classified into high (DAS28-ESR ˃5.1) and non-high (DAS28-ESR ≤5.1) disease activity groups. Complete blood count, serum albumin, and C-reactive protein (CRP) were measured to calculate CAR, PAR, and PNI. Rheumatoid arthritis patients had higher CAR and PAR, but lower PNI compared with controls (all p < 0.001). Patients with high disease activity had higher CAR and PAR, but lower PNI than those with non-high disease activity (p < 0.001, p=0.001, p=0.018 respectively). CAR and PAR correlated positively with DAS28-ESR, ESR and CRP, whereas PNI correlated negatively with these inflammatory measures. CAR showed the highest diagnostic performance for identifying RA patients (AUC=0.873), followed by PNI and PAR. CAR showed significantly superior performance, with no significant difference between PAR and PNI. CAR also showed the highest discriminatory performance for high disease activity (AUC=0.676) followed by PAR and PNI, although differences among them were not statistically significant. Higher CAR and PAR, whereas lower PNI were significantly associated with increased odds of high disease activity. Only CAR remained an independent predictor (p=0.005) in multivariate analysis. In conclusion, CAR, PAR, and PNI are available composite biomarkers that provide complementary information regarding inflammatory burden and nutritional status in RA patients, with CAR showing the greatest utility.

items.title: Immunological cross-talk between periodontitis and systemic lupus erythematosus: the role of T-B cell dysregulation in the shared pathogenic network.
items.abstract: Periodontitis and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) exhibit overlapping immunopathological features characterized by dysregulated adaptive immune responses. Emerging evidence suggests that aberrant T-B cell crosstalk represents a potential immunological link between chronic oral inflammation and systemic autoimmunity. Persistent periodontal inflammation promotes the release of pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) and damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), leading to dendritic cell activation, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, and sustained immune stimulation. These signals may facilitate abnormal germinal center responses through enhanced Tfh-B cell interactions and increased BAFF and IL-21 signaling, thereby amplifying B-cell activation, plasma-cell differentiation, and antibody production. Conversely, SLE-associated systemic immune dysregulation may aggravate periodontal inflammation, suggesting a potentially bidirectional interaction between oral and systemic immunity. However, most available evidence has been obtained from separate studies of periodontitis and SLE and does not establish a shared causal pathway between the two diseases. In this review, we summarize current evidence supporting the role of T-B cell dysregulation as a potential immunological link between periodontitis and SLE. We further discuss candidate mechanisms involving dendritic cells, NETs, BAFF, IL-21, and germinal center reactions, as well as their therapeutic implications. Elucidating the oral-systemic immune axis may provide novel insights into integrated immunomodulatory strategies for autoimmune diseases.

items.title: Joint-brain communication in rheumatoid arthritis: glial mechanisms, pain phenotypes, and translational evidence.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic autoimmune disease in which persistent pain, fatigue, cognitive impairment, depression, and anxiety may involve altered central nervous system (CNS) processing. This narrative review synthesizes preclinical and clinical evidence concerning proposed glial cell-mediated joint-brain communication in RA. Joint-derived neural inputs and systemic inflammatory signals may communicate with the CNS through humoral, cellular, neural, neuroendocrine, and neurovascular pathways. Preclinical studies implicate microglia and astrocytes in neuroinflammatory responses, spinal central sensitization, impaired hippocampal plasticity, and neurovascular alterations. Human studies associate systemic inflammation with altered brain connectivity and CNS-related symptoms. Disease-modifying antirheumatic treatment, particularly tumor necrosis factor inhibition, has been associated with improvements in selected CNS-related outcomes. Adjunctive symptom management includes phenotype-guided analgesic approaches, rehabilitation, and psychological and sleep-focused interventions. Translational research explores glial modulators, pathway-specific interventions, vagal neuromodulation, neuroimaging, cerebrospinal fluid markers, and multidimensional patient stratification. The proposed joint-brain framework highlights the value of assessing inflammation alongside pain phenotype, cognition, mood, fatigue, sleep, and function. Future human studies should evaluate whether mechanistic and biomarker findings can improve individualized treatment selection and clinical outcomes.

items.title: Targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome in rheumatoid arthritis fibroblast-like synoviocytes: pathogenic mechanisms, therapeutic strategies, and translational perspectives.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic systemic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent synovitis, pannus formation, cartilage degradation, and bone erosion. Although conventional synthetic, biologic, and targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs have improved disease control, many patients fail to achieve sustained remission, lose responsiveness over time, or develop treatment-limiting safety concerns. Fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLSs) are increasingly recognized as long-lived pathogenic stromal cells that sustain synovial inflammation, promote matrix degradation, support osteoclastogenesis, and shape immune and vascular crosstalk within the rheumatoid joint. The NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome provides a mechanistic link between synovial stress responses and inflammatory amplification. In RA-FLSs, defined inflammatory, hypoxic and oxidative-stress conditions can induce NLRP3-related signaling, whereas other proposed triggers, including lysosomal injury, extracellular ATP and ion flux, are supported more strongly by broader synovial or general inflammasome evidence. Through caspase-1 activation, interleukin (IL)-1β and IL-18 maturation, and gasdermin D-mediated pyroptotic signaling, NLRP3 can reinforce stromal inflammation and tissue-destructive synovial remodeling. In this review, we summarize canonical, non-canonical, and alternative mechanisms of NLRP3 inflammasome activation, with emphasis on their relevance to RA-FLS biology and the inflamed synovial niche. We discuss how NLRP3 signaling intersects with fibroblast heterogeneity, macrophage-FLS crosstalk, endothelial activation, chondrocyte injury, osteoclastogenesis, and context-dependent pyroptosis. We further evaluate pharmacological strategies targeting the NLRP3 axis, including direct NLRP3 inhibitors, upstream stress modulators, caspase-1 or gasdermin D blockade, IL-1β/IL-18 pathway inhibition, natural products, repurposed molecules, nanomedicine-based delivery, and rational combination regimens. Key translational issues include FLS specificity, synovial drug exposure, target engagement, chronic safety, biomarker-guided patient selection, and mechanism-aligned endpoints. An RA-FLS-centered view of NLRP3 targeting may help refine anti-inflammatory pharmacology and support the development of synovium-directed therapeutic strategies for selected patients with difficult-to-treat RA.

items.title: Case Report: Orbital and intracranial inflammatory syndrome in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: To describe a case of rheumatoid arthritis (RA)-associated orbital and intracranial inflammatory disorder (OIID). RA is a systemic autoimmune disease associated with a multitude of extra-articular manifestations. Cigarette smoking increases the risk of RA vasculitis and adversely influences the expression of the proto-oncogene p53 in RA. Although ocular manifestations of RA are well known, orbital and intracranial inflammatory presentations are much less common. A 63-year-old woman with seropositive RA and a significant tobacco smoking history presented with intermittent jaw pain, headache, left temporal tenderness, blurred vision of the left eye, and intermittent diplopia. Serum laboratory studies demonstrated elevated RF and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). Cranial and orbital magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed left orbital apex enhancement with extension into the left cavernous sinus and Meckel cave. The patient improved with intravenous methylprednisolone and high-dose prednisone, but symptoms recurred with each steroid taper. 13 months later, the patient developed new contralateral right-sided orbital inflammation with cavernous sinus and superior orbital fissure involvement. Clinicians should be aware that orbital (e.g., orbital inflammatory pseudotumor) and intracranial presentations may occur in RA in addition to the more common ocular (e.g., scleritis) presentations.

items.title: Recurrent Pericarditis With Cardiac Tamponade in a Patient With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Case Report.
items.abstract: A 29-year-old male with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) with class IV/V lupus nephritis, recurrent pericardial effusions, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus presented for worsening chest tightness and shortness of breath. Echocardiography revealed a large, free-flowing pericardial effusion circumferential to the heart, up to 2.9 cm at its widest diameter, with mild atrial and right ventricular collapse. Due to concern for tamponade, interventional cardiology was consulted, and a pericardiocentesis was performed, yielding 820 mL of serosanguinous fluid, and a pericardial drain was kept in place. Given his history of SLE, immunosuppressive therapy was started with intravenous methylprednisolone pulse dosing 250 mg twice a day for three days, followed by an oral prednisone taper and mycophenolate mofetil 500 mg twice a day titrating up to 1500 mg twice a day, as well as increasing hydroxychloroquine to 400 mg daily from 200 mg daily, starting colchicine 0.6 mg daily, and continuing voclosporin 23.7 mg twice a day. However, his pericardial effusion persisted, ultimately requiring a pericardial window. Unfortunately, just a few weeks later, he returned again with recurrent pleuropericarditis in spite of aggressive medical and surgical management and ultimately elected to leave against medical advice. This case highlights the challenges in managing recurrent pericardial effusions in patients with SLE.

items.title: When Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis (EGPA) Looks Like Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis (GPA): Navigating a Complex Case of Anti-neutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibodies (ANCA) Vasculitis.
items.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is an anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis, with myeloperoxidase antibodies in 40% of cases. Proteinase 3 (PR3) positivity is rare and may overlap with granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA). We present a 43-year-old male with recurrent sinusitis, epistaxis, neuropathic pain, and acute kidney injury, with histopathology of kidney biopsy showing EGPA despite the absence of asthma, which is rare. His PR3 positivity and clinical presentation mimicked GPA, highlighting the diagnostic challenges of vasculitides. We report this case to highlight that EGPA can have an atypical presentation. PR3-ANCA positivity and absence of asthma do not exclude EGPA. Also, renal biopsy is crucial for diagnosis when serology and clinical features do not align.

items.title: Late-onset ankylosing spondylitis presenting with severe flank and abdominal-to-back pain in a 64-year-old man: a case report.
items.abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory disease that primarily affects the spine and sacroiliac joints and is typically diagnosed in younger adults. However, AS may be overlooked in older patients when symptoms are atypically localized, such as flank or abdominal-to-back pain, rather than classic inflammatory low back pain. We report the case of a 64-year-old man who presented with persistent left-sided abdominal-to-back pain accompanied by markedly elevated inflammatory markers. Initial evaluation focused on abdominal, urinary, infectious, malignant, and degenerative spinal disorders. However, imaging revealed bilateral grade 3 sacroiliitis according to the modified New York criteria, marked narrowing and partial anterior fusion of both sacroiliac joints on pelvic computed tomography (CT), and lumbar vertebral corner ossification. Human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-B27 was negative. Based on the overall clinical and radiographic findings, late-onset AS was diagnosed. After diagnosis, adalimumab (ADA) was initiated and rapidly improved disease activity. Because its efficacy later waned, treatment was switched to infliximab (IFX), which restored disease control. Although disease activity worsened after switching to an IFX biosimilar, reintroduction of originator IFX restored clinical remission, which was maintained for 2.5 years without serious adverse events. This case highlights that late-onset AS may present with atypical flank and abdominal-to-back pain rather than classic inflammatory low back pain. In older patients with unexplained persistent flank or abdominal-to-back pain and markedly elevated inflammatory markers, AS should be considered in the differential diagnosis after excluding abdominal, urinary, infectious, malignant, and degenerative spinal disorders. Careful differentiation from diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH) is particularly important when extensive spinal ossification is present.

items.title: Ocular Manifestations and Visual Outcomes of Patients with Giant Cell Arteritis.
items.abstract: Ocular involvement in giant cell arteritis (GCA) is common, yet there is limited literature addressing its specific ocular manifestations and their impact on visual outcomes. The objective was to evaluate the incidence of visual involvement, treatment, relapse rate, and visual outcome in patients with GCA. This is a single center retrospective cohort study. The study included 35 eyes from 37 consecutive patients with biopsy-proven GCA (TAB+), 39 eyes from 39 consecutive patients with clinically diagnosed GCA and negative biopsy (TAB-), and 16 eyes from 21 consecutive patients clinically diagnosed with GCA without undergoing a biopsy (no TAB). We collected demographic and clinical presentation. 26/37 (70%) in the TAB+ group, 29/39 (74%) in the TAB- group, and 14/21 (67%) in the no TAB group underwent at least one neuro-ophthalmic exam. Eyes were grouped into no, mild, or severe ocular involvement. At each visit, patients underwent neuro-ophthalmic evaluation, ophthalmic imaging, and visual fields. The main outcome measures were best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), color perception (% correct), retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), ganglion cell complex (GCC), area of foveal avascular zone (FAZ), and Humphrey visual field (HVF). Within our entire cohort of 97 patients, 69 (71%) underwent neuro-ophthalmic examinations, 5 had unilateral involvement and 42 had bilateral involvement. At diagnosis, all patients were started on high dose prednisone, 9/37 (24%) intravenously and 28/37 (76%) orally. 16/37 (43%) patients were treated with adjuvant tocilizumab. Within our cohort, 5/97 (5%) patients had visual relapses, all within the first year after diagnosis. 15/50 (30%) eyes had no OI, 22/50 (44%) eyes had mild OI, and 13/50 (26%) eyes had severe OI. After 12 months of GCA diagnosis, patients with no OI compared to severe OI demonstrated: BCVA (logMAR 0.164 vs. 1.26, p<0.001), color perception (87% vs 6%, p<0.001), RNFL (93μm vs. 56μm, p<0.001), GCC (76μm vs. 52μm, p<0.001), FAZ (0.119 mm 2 vs. 0.314 mm 2 , p<0.001), and HVF (-2.58 vs. -19.18, p<0.001). Visual involvement in GCA is common. The affected eyes had irreversible vision loss. GCC, RNFL, and FAZ were associated with poor visual outcome.

items.title: Acid-responsive nanoparticles with microneedles for anti‑inflammatory sonodynamic therapy of gouty arthritis.
items.abstract: The pathological microenvironment of acute gouty arthritis (AGA) features local tissue acidification and the release of a storm of pro-inflammatory cytokines. To address this dual challenge, we engineered an acid-responsive curcumin-loaded nanoparticles microneedle system (Cur-PNPs@MN) that delivers curcumin with pH-triggered release and anti-inflammatory activity. This integrated platform combines a hyaluronic acid (HA)-based dissolving microneedle for localized transdermal delivery of acid-degradable PCADK (poly (cyclohexane-1,4-diyl acetone dimethylene ketal)) curcumin nanoparticles (Cur-PNPs), which are designed for pH-triggered curcumin release at the pathological site. Together, they deliver curcumin, a dual-function agent acting both as an anti-inflammatory compound and a nanoenhanced sonosensitizer. In vitro , the system exhibited acid-responsive drug release and also promoted macrophage uptake, achieving significant curcumin accumulation within 1 hour and saturation by 4 hours. Moreover, it could generate potent ultrasound-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS). The ROS generation capability of Cur-PNPs was 1.47-fold higher than that of Cur‑aggregates, resulting in anapoptosis rate of 29.9% in M1 macrophages. In vivo, the chemo-sonodynamic therapy (Cur-PNPs@MN+Ultrasound (US)) in a rat AGA model significantly alleviated joint swelling and inflammatory infiltration, while drastically suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines, with IL-1β decreasing from 170.3 to 67.3 pg/mL, TNF- α from 20.8 to 5.9 pg/mL, and IL-6 from 140.9 to 48.2 pg/mL, and achieved therapeutic efficacy comparable to conventional drugs. This work demonstrates a synergistic chemo‑sonodynamic strategy by coupling pH-triggered curcumin release with ultrasound-enhanced ROS generation. This acid-responsive therapeutic strategy enhances anti-inflammatory efficacy and reduction of M1-associated inflammatory responses, offering an effective approach for AGA therapy.

items.title: Multimodal Profiling of Complement Expression and Association With Outcomes in ANCA-Associated Vasculitis With Glomerulonephritis.
items.abstract: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV) with glomerulonephritis (AAV-GN) is classically considered pauci-immune, yet complement activation is a central pathogenic mechanism. Whether intrarenal complement-related transcriptional programs are reflected by conventional serum or immunofluorescence markers, and whether they are clinically informative, remains unclear. In 369 patients with AAV-GN from 2 independent retrospective cohorts, complement was assessed across circulating, histopathologic, and transcriptomic layers (serum C3/C4, glomerular C1q/C3 deposition, and targeted kidney transcriptomics). Predefined classical and alternative pathway-related expression scores were derived from intrarenal gene expression. Associations with severity and outcomes were evaluated using multivariable Cox models. Public spatial transcriptomic data sets provided validation and localization. Below-normal serum C3/C4 levels were uncommon. Low serum C3, but not C4, was associated with more severe kidney involvement, kidney failure (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]: 2.0 [1.1-3.7]), and mortality (aHR: 2.3 [1.3-4.0]). Both glomerular C3 (47%) and C1q (11%) deposition identified more severe pathology and adverse outcomes. Compared with controls, AAV-GN kidneys showed increased complement-related expression-including classical pathway components, proximal alternative pathway genes ( C3 , C5AR1) , and regulatory transcripts-that was only weakly concordant with serum or deposition markers. Low alternative pathway-related expression was independently associated with better kidney (aHR: 0.3 [0.1-0.7]) and overall (aHR: 0.4 [0.2-0.9]) survival. Spatial transcriptomics validated these signatures and suggested contributions from both immune and resident kidney compartments. AAV-GN displays a reproducible intrarenal complement-related transcriptional program, only weakly captured by serum levels or routine immunofluorescence, associated with renal severity and outcomes. These findings support prospective studies integrating tissue complement transcriptomics for stratification and therapeutic hypothesis generation.

items.title: Higher APOB is associated with poor renal outcome in lupus nephritis.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis is a common and severe complication of SLE, significantly affecting patient morbidity and mortality. It is quite meaningful to identify some non-invasive predictors related to the progression of LN. Early intervention of these factors may delay the development to ESRD. This study included 462 LN patients at The Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University from January 2018 to September 2023. The participants were divided into two groups: high APOB group (serum APOB > 0.8 g/L, n = 264) and the low APOB group (serum APOB ≤ 0.8 g/L, n = 198) according to the median baseline serum APOB concentration. The results demonstrated that LN patients in the high APOB group had significantly higher lipid metabolism-related indicators (P < 0.001), higher levels of urea, SUA, and SCr (P < 0.01), and a higher proportion of patients with CKD stages 3-4 (P = 0.011). The Kaplan-Meier survival curve showed that the high APOB group patients had worse renal prognosis (HR = 3.292, 95%CI: 1.835-5.907, P < 0.001). To investigate the impact of long-term APOB exposure, this study also collected various APOB exposure metrics in the cumAPOB cohort which included 286 LN patients. The statistical results showed that compared with the low cumAPOB group, the lipid metabolism-related indexes (P < 0.001) and the proportion of patients who reached endpoints (P = 0.001) in the high cumAPOB group were significantly higher. And the cumAPOB was a risk factor for poor renal prognosis in patients with LN. When the high APOB exposure time reached 3 years, the risk of endpoint events was approximately 15 times that of the control group (OR = 15.08, 95%CI 2.159-105.3, P = 0.006). Serum APOB level may be positively associated with the poor renal progression of LN. Key Points • Renal biopsy plays a key role in the evaluation and management of lupus nephritis (LN). However, some patients may not accept this detection for its invasive procedure. Therefore, it is quite meaningful to identify risk factors related to the progression of LN in some non-invasive method. • With the prolonged high-exposure duration of APOB, the risk of endpoint events in LN patients within the cohort gradually increased. • The impact of APOB on the renal prognosis of LN patients was not instantaneous, but results from long-term high-level cumulative exposure - a slow process of quantitative to qualitative change. • APOB was an independent risk factor for LN patients, with a cumulative effect.

items.title: Osteoporosis and fracture severity as independent risk factors for osteonecrosis of the jaw in rheumatoid arthritis: a TriNetX cohort study.
items.abstract: To investigate the independent impact of osteoporosis and its severity, characterised by bone fractures, on osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ) risk in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) using a global real-world database. We hypothesised that osteoporosis independently increases ONJ risk in patients with RA, irrespective of medication exposure. This retrospective cohort study utilised the TriNetX database. Primary analysis estimated the association between osteoporosis and incident ONJ (primary outcome) after propensity score matching (PSM). Secondary analysis evaluated the impact of bone fractures using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Sensitivity analyses assessed robustness. In the primary PSM analysis (160,789 pairs), osteoporosis was the strongest independent risk factor for ONJ (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 3.135, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.740-3.584, P < 0.001). Among patients with osteoporosis (22,821 pairs), ONJ incidence was higher in those with bone fractures (P = 0.047). Multivariable analysis identified bone fractures (aHR 1.522, 95% CI 1.202-1.931, P < 0.001) and denosumab use (aHR 1.970, 95% CI 1.397-2.777, P < 0.001) as independent risk factors. Sensitivity analyses confirmed that the association between osteoporosis and ONJ remained robust in antiresorptive-naïve and glucocorticoid-naïve patients after excluding bone metastasis and high-dose antiresorptive therapy (aHR 3.125, 95% CI 2.564-3.817, P < 0.0001). Osteoporosis and fracture history are independent risk factors for ONJ in patients with RA. These findings support a disease-driven paradigm where underlying bone fragility drives ONJ development beyond antiresorptive or glucocorticoid effects, highlighting the need for comprehensive bone health management in this population. Future prospective studies are needed to evaluate targeted screening interventions. Key points • Osteoporosis is a stronger independent risk factor for ONJ than antiresorptive medication. • Prior bone fractures significantly increase ONJ risk among patients with rheumatoid arthritis and osteoporosis. • Managing underlying bone fragility is crucial for ONJ prevention, beyond monitoring osteoporosis medication use.

items.title: Seizures as a marker of severe multi-organ involvement in neuropsychiatric systemic lupus erythematosus: a diagnostic risk stratification study.
items.abstract: This study aimed to identify independent predictors of seizure occurrence in patients with neuropsychiatric systemic lupus erythematosus (NPSLE), develop a diagnostic model, and evaluate whether seizures are associated with adverse renal outcomes. A retrospective cohort of 169 patients with NPSLE from Xiangya Hospital was analyzed. Among 70 pre-specified clinical, laboratory, and imaging variables, 20 variables associated with seizure occurrence (p < 0.05 in univariable logistic regression) were retained after multicollinearity screening (VIF < 5.0). Multivariable logistic regression was then performed to identify independent predictors of SE-NPSLE. Machine learning algorithms with fivefold cross-validation were then employed to develop and optimize the diagnostic model. Model performance was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and AUC metrics. External validation was performed using an independent cohort (n = 46) from Jiangsu Provincial People's Hospital. Renal survival rates were assessed by Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank tests. Independent predictors of SE-NPSLE included anti-Rib-P antibody (OR = 0.315, 95% CI: 0.121-0.819), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) (OR = 0.973 per mm/h, 95% CI: 0.954-0.992), and presence of psychosis (OR = 0.194, 95% CI: 0.057-0.659). A logistic regression-based nomogram (AUC: 0.818 training, 0.800 validation) demonstrated robust performance. External validation (n = 46) yielded an AUC of 0.706. What is more, NPSLE patients with seizures (SE-NPSLE) demonstrated significantly worse renal outcomes compared to NPSLE patients without seizures (non-SE-NPSLE). Seizures in NPSLE are associated with poor renal prognosis. Our diagnostic model was developed to facilitate early risk assessment and may aid personalized seizure management; however, its clinical utility requires validation in larger, prospective cohorts. Key Points • A validated diagnostic model indentifies high-risk NPSLE patients for seizures. • 3 independent predictors of SE-NPSLE included anti-Rib-P antibodies, ESR and psychosis. • SE-NPSLE patients were youner, had higher SLEDAI, and exhibited more severe renal dysfunction than non-SE-NPSLE patients.

items.title: The mystery of BMI in Sjögren's disease: unravelling complex relationships between BMI and multiple laboratory parameters.
items.abstract: The relationship between body mass index (BMI) and laboratory parameters in Sjögren's disease (SjD) remains unclear. We evaluated associations of BMI with selected serological and haematological parameters and explored its relationship with the EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI). This single-centre retrospective cross-sectional study included 554 unique hospitalised patients with SjD. Multivariable linear regression models were adjusted for age, sex and disease duration. Effect estimates were expressed per 5 kg/m² higher BMI, and Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction was applied across all estimable laboratory outcomes. Generalised additive and segmented regression models examined nonlinear relationships. Natural-log-transformed CRP and TNF-α analyses and an ESSDAI score excluding both biological and haematological domains were used as sensitivity analyses. After adjustment for age, sex and disease duration, each 5 kg/m² higher BMI was associated with lower IgG and higher C3, HGB, WBC and RBC after false discovery rate correction. CRP showed a nominal inverse association (P = 0.038, q = 0.076). TNF-α showed no linear association, but U-shaped patterns were observed in raw and log-transformed analyses. BMI was weakly inversely correlated with ESSDAI (ρ=-0.160, P < 0.001) and very weakly with ESSDAI excluding the biological and haematological domains (ρ=-0.085, P = 0.044). BMI was associated with several laboratory parameters and weakly with ESSDAI in this hypothesis-generating cross-sectional study. The underlying mechanisms remain uncertain.

items.title: Upregulated ST2L-Dependent IL-33 Signaling in Dermal Fibroblasts Contributes to IL-6 Induction and Skin Fibrosis in Systemic Sclerosis.
items.abstract: Persistent activation of dermal fibroblasts drives progressive skin fibrosis in systemic sclerosis (SSc), a connective tissue disease. However, the mechanisms sustaining fibroblast activation remain incompletely defined. Interleukin-33 (IL-33), an alarmin-like IL-1 family cytokine, signals via the membrane receptor ST2L along with IL1RAP to activate pathways such as NF-κB, whereas soluble ST2 (sST2) acts as a decoy. The contribution of this axis to skin fibrosis in SSc is unclear. This study was aimed at defining the expression and functional significance of IL-33/ST2L signaling in SSc dermal fibroblasts and experimental dermal fibrosis. IL-33, ST2L, sST2, and IL1RAP expression in cultured dermal fibroblasts and skin samples from patients with diffuse cutaneous SSc and healthy donors was estimated via quantitative real-time PCR and immunoblotting. In vivo relevance of the findings was assessed using a bleomycin-induced skin fibrosis model in IL-33 knockout mice, via histology (hematoxylin and eosin and Masson's trichrome staining), dermal thickness measurements, collagen quantification (Sircol assay), and IL-6 mRNA analysis. At the cellular level, causality was examined by lentiviral overexpression of ST2L in control fibroblasts and its small interfering RNA-mediated knockdown in SSc fibroblasts, with recombinant IL-33 stimulation and readouts, including IL-6 induction and IκBα phosphorylation. IL-33 and ST2L were significantly upregulated in cultured SSc fibroblasts, whereas sST2 and IL1RAP expression was unchanged. Bleomycin increased IL-33 and ST2L expression in mouse skin, and IL-33 deficiency attenuated dermal thickening, collagen accumulation, and IL-6 induction. Mechanistically, ST2L overexpression rendered control fibroblasts IL-33-responsive, inducing IL-6 and transient IκBα phosphorylation, whereas ST2L knockdown reduced basal IL-6 levels and blunted IL-33-induced IL-6 expression in SSc fibroblasts. These results indicate that elevated ST2L expression amplifies IL-33 responsiveness in SSc dermal fibroblasts and promotes IL-6 production via NF-κB signaling, implicating the IL-33/ST2L axis as a contributor to fibrotic skin remodeling and a potential therapeutic target in SSc.

items.title: Multiple cranial neuropathies in a patient with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
items.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a rare vasculitis characterised by asthma, eosinophilia and sinonasal disease. Although peripheral neuropathy is common, central nervous system involvement occurs in only 3%–5% of patients and may cause significant morbidity. We present an older adult male with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-negative EGPA, that relapsed after discontinuing mepolizumab and developed sequential cranial neuropathies involving cranial nerves V, VII, II and X, causing trigeminal neuropathy, bilateral facial palsy, optic neuropathy and vocal cord dysfunction. MRI demonstrated hypertrophic pachymeningitis (HP) with multifocal pachymeningeal enhancement. The patient received pulse intravenous methylprednisolone followed by cyclophosphamide infusion, resulting in headache resolution, stabilisation of visual symptoms, improvement in hoarseness and decreased pachymeningeal enhancement on follow-up MRI. He was transitioned to methotrexate and monthly mepolizumab maintenance therapy. This case highlights a rare presentation of EGPA with sequential multiple cranial neuropathies secondary to HP, emphasising the importance of early recognition and aggressive immunosuppressive therapy.

items.title: JAK Inhibitor Cycling Shows Higher Drug Retention than Biologic Switching Following First JAK Inhibitor Failure in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Evidence guiding treatment sequencing after JAK inhibitor failure in rheumatoid arthritis remains limited. This study compared treatment persistence and clinical effectiveness between JAK inhibitor cycling and biologic switching after discontinuation of an initial JAK inhibitor due to inadequate response. This multicenter retrospective cohort study included only patients who discontinued their first JAK inhibitor due to inadequate response. The primary outcome was 12-month drug retention. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was used to balance baseline characteristics. Secondary outcomes included reasons for discontinuation within 12 months and clinical effectiveness at 6 months, assessed using the response criteria of the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology. Among the 186 patients, 44 (23.7%) cycled to another JAK inhibitor and 142 (76.3%) switched to biologic therapy. After adjustment using inverse probability of treatment weighting, cycling was associated with significantly higher 12-month drug retention than switching (hazard ratio, 0.27; 95% CI, 0.10-0.71; P < 0.01). This difference was mainly driven by fewer discontinuations owing to insufficient efficacy. Concomitant glucocorticoid use independently predicted improved retention (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.28-0.92; P < 0.05). At 6 months, good or moderate response rates were not significantly different between groups (78.6% vs. 62.0%), although multivariable analysis favored cycling (odds ratio, 3.41; 95% CI, 1.03-11.29; P < 0.05). Among patients with rheumatoid arthritis who had an inadequate response to their first JAK inhibitor, cycling to another JAK inhibitor was associated with superior 12-month drug retention with comparable short-term clinical effectiveness.

items.title: The Relationship Between Pan Immune-Inflammation Value and Disease Activity in Ankylosing Spondylitis.
items.abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory disease affecting the axial skeleton and peripheral joints, causing pain, stiffness, and reduced function. Monitoring disease activity is crucial, but no specific laboratory markers reflect disease activity in AS. This study evaluated the relationship between pan immune-inflammation value (PIIV) and disease activity in AS. This study included patients with AS fulfilling the modified New York classification criteria. Disease activity was assessed using the Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI) and the Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score with C-reactive protein (ASDAS-CRP). Data included demographic, clinical, treatment, and laboratory variables, including C-reactive protein (CRP), erythrocyte sedimentation rate, blood counts, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and PIIV. Of 64 patients (female/male: 22/42), 38 (59.4%) had active disease according to BASDAI. The active group showed higher PIIV, ASDAS-CRP, platelet count, PLR, and SII, and lower hemoglobin than the inactive group. PIIV correlated with BASDAI, ASDAS-CRP, and inflammatory markers including CRP, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, neutrophil, platelet, and monocyte counts, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, PLR, monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio, and SII. PIIV was significantly higher in active AS and correlated with disease activity and inflammatory markers. It may support disease activity assessment in AS.

items.title: Clusters of GSDMD and GSDME mediate neutrophil pyroptosis in cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome.
items.abstract: The Nod-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome is a cytosolic multiprotein immune sensor that is restrained from assembling at steady state. Mutations in NLRP3 associated with cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome (CAPS) enhance inflammasome formation and activation, resulting in neutrophil-predominant systemic and tissue inflammation. Here, we investigated how gasdermin D (GSDMD) and GSDME drive interleukin-1β (IL-1β) release, pyroptosis, and autoinflammation during constitutive and canonical NLRP3 activation in neutrophils. Mass cytometry analysis of neutrophils from patients with CAPS revealed heterogeneous subtypes with differing amounts of intracellular IL-1β. In mice, neutrophil-specific expression of activating Nlrp3 mutations orthologous to those in patients with CAPS uncovered nonredundant roles for GSDMD and GSDME downstream of inflammasome activation. Combined deletion of Gsdmd and Gsdme in these CAPS models reduced IL-1β secretion, prevented pyroptosis, and mitigated autoinflammation. Loss of both GSDMD and GSDME reduced caspase-1 cleavage and pro-IL-1β processing downstream of NLRP3 activation, whereas GSDMD deficiency alone increased cleavage of GSDME and caspase-8. Clusters of GSDMD and GSDME were closely associated with one another at the plasma membrane of activated neutrophils from CAPS mice. These findings indicate that the coordinated actions of membrane-associated GSDMD and GSDME reinforce cytosolic NLRP3 inflammasome activation to promote IL-1β secretion, lytic cell death, and autoinflammation.

items.title: Vigorous physical activity and physical function are strongly associated with better health in patients with long-standing radiographic axial spondyloarthritis.
items.abstract: To evaluate the impact of physical function and level of physical activity on health status and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in patients with long-standing radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (r-axSpA). In total, 141 patients with long-standing r-axSpA were included in this cross-sectional cohort study. Assessments included physical function (Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index (BASFI)), spinal mobility (modified Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Metrology Index (BASMI)), muscle function for leg strength (Timed Stands Test (TST)) and handgrip force (Grippit), amount of self-reported physical activity (vigorous physical activity, moderate physical activity, sedentary behavior), health status by ASAS Health Index (ASAS HI) and HRQoL with Short Form Survey Instrument 36-Item. Multivariable linear regression was used to analyze associations between health status, HRQoL, physical activity, muscle function, and physical function. The mean (SD) age was 60 (12) years, diagnosis duration was 25 (10) years, and 57% were male. Physical function and vigorous physical activity were the strongest determinants of health status and HRQoL. The models explained approximately 50% of the variation in ASAS HI and the physical aspects of HRQoL and 21% of the mental aspects of HRQoL. Participants displayed good health status (62%) by ASAS HI ≤ 5, reached the recommended level of health-enhancing physical activity (77%), had normal muscle function (TST 82% and Grippit 91%), and demonstrated physical function (55%), and spinal mobility (45%) within reference values. This study highlights the importance of regular vigorous physical activity in older individuals living with long-standing r-axSpA since it was strongly associated with health status and HRQoL.

items.title: Geroprotective efficacy of Triphalaguggul: a polyherbal formulation against inflammatory disorders through inhibition of pro-inflammatory cytokines as therapeutic biomarkers.
items.abstract: Due to increase in life expectancy, aged population is growing exponentially, globally which has impact on human health as well as biomedical research. Research highlighted coordination between aging and arthritis where aging is the underlying hallmark of arthritis progression. Despite knowing the route of pathogenesis regarding most prevalent joint disorders like Osteoarthritis (OA) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA); efficient curable approach is still challenging. Worldwide 7-8% populations suffer from OA while 0.2-1% people are invaded by RA. Due to high cost, inadequate pharmacological action and adverse effects, NSAIDs are considered as secondary treatment option. Today, demographic changes towards polyherbal medicine usage targeting inhibition of pro-inflammatory cytokines are the challenge of the day. This study focused on Triphalaguggul (TG); a polyherbal formulation for treatment of arthritis targeting down regulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines and its signaling pathways. Toxicology study along with anti-OA and anti-RA evaluation in MIA and CFA induced rat model respectively. TG could reduce 96.15% inflamed knee, 95.18% paw edema and also helped in regrowth and rearrangement of chondrocytes properly in OA. In arthritic condition, increased hematological parameters like SGPT, SGOT, AlkP, CRP, RF were reinstated to normal range after treatment (p < 0.05). ELISA revealed that elevated IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β were decreased after drug treatment (p < 0.05). Enhanced expression of p-JAK2, p-STAT3, NFκβ/p65 were downregulated (p < 0.05) after treatment which was validated by western blot and immunohistochemistry. Finding suggested that TG exhibited anti-arthritic activity down-regulating pro-inflammatory cytokines, JAK/STAT and NFƘβ signaling pathway as a therapeutic biomarker to protect from geriatric disease.

items.title: Donor-aware integrative single-cell analysis distinguishes consistent memory B-cell programmes from donor-sensitive state boundaries in untreated rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Single-cell transcriptomics resolves immune-cell heterogeneity, but whether cluster boundaries or coordinated programmes are the more transferable unit across donors remains uncertain. We reanalyzed 14,414 circulating memory B cells from four untreated rheumatoid arthritis donors. Harmony increased mean local donor entropy from 0.506 to 0.912, while original labels showed only moderate agreement with uncorrected and Harmony reclustering (adjusted Rand indices 0.508 and 0.473). Conditional label permutations and analyses based on pan-B-centred residuals or state-marker genes supported donor-level consistency for most major states, but identified C3-PECAM1 and the rare C10-IFN state as weakly specific or quality-control-sensitive. In training-only donor-held-out transfer, accuracy was 66.0-70.5% and adjusted Rand index was 0.432-0.525, indicating partial transfer rather than independent state recovery. Removal of DoubletFinder-predicted doublets preserved 15-20 of each state's top 20 pseudobulk markers and did not change programme rank order across states. Rank-based UCell scores agreed with AddModuleScore in both datasets. In an independent cohort of 5,725 memory B cells from 34 donors, adapted programme scores could be quantified, but no disease-activity or serological association remained significant after correction; treatment and unavailable disease-duration data limited clinical interpretation. These results distinguish recurrent donor-level transcriptional structure from analysis-sensitive state boundaries and support programme-level interpretation without claiming independent cell-state validation or biomarker utility.

items.title: Performance of the Expanded Cardiovascular Risk Prediction Score for Rheumatoid Arthritis: An External Validation in the BRASS Registry.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular (CV) disease occurs more frequently in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) than in the general population and is difficult to predict. The expanded risk score for RA (ERS-RA) has demonstrated good discrimination and calibration in prior studies, but additional external validation studies are needed to understand clinical utility. Data from a single center RA registry was integrated with electronic health records (EHR) and linked to Medicare/Medicaid administrative claims data. A less restrictive CV outcome was defined as an event identified in any of the three data sources (questionnaires/EHR/claims), and a more restrictive outcome included events in EHR and claims. External validation of the ERS-RA examined model discrimination and calibration. The longitudinal RA registry has 1,332 participants aged 20-80 years without prior evidence of CVD, followed for a mean of 6.8 years. The mean age was 54 years and 84% were female. We observed 164 (12.3%) and 69 (5.2%) participants with a CV event with the less and more restrictive CV definitions, respectively. The mean ERS-RA predicted score was 7.1%, and 424 (32%) participants had a predictive score ≥7.5%. We observed c-statistics of 0.66 (95% CI 0.62-0.71; less restrictive) and 0.80 (95% CI 0.76-0.85; more restrictive). The ERS-RA also demonstrated good calibration, with better performance for the more restrictive CV event definition. The ERS-RA demonstrated good discrimination and calibration for CV risk prediction in an external validation RA cohort. It also highlights the importance of using multiple sources of data to find CV events in a non-CV registry.

items.title: Disseminated Herpes Simplex Virus Infection Presenting With Cytopenias in a Patient With Untreated Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Disseminated herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection is an uncommon but serious condition, typically seen in immunocompromised hosts. Cytopenias, including neutropenia and thrombocytopenia, are rare manifestations, particularly in patients not actively receiving immunosuppressive therapy. We report a 75-year-old female with a history of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), previously on methotrexate and low-dose prednisone, who presented with painful oral and genital ulcers, mucositis, and rapidly progressive bicytopenia (neutropenia and thrombocytopenia). Her recent brief reinitiation of methotrexate prompted evaluation for drug-induced cytopenias; however, methotrexate levels were undetectable. Extensive infectious, nutritional, rheumatologic, and hematologic workup revealed HSV positivity from oral and inguinal ulcers. Bone marrow biopsy showed no evidence of hematologic malignancy or aplasia. She was treated with intravenous acyclovir, leading to clinical improvement and recovery of blood counts. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of cytopenias in patients with autoimmune diseases. While methotrexate toxicity and Felty's syndrome were initially considered, the clinical trajectory and lack of supportive findings redirected focus to infectious causes. Disseminated HSV infection causing cytopenias is rare and often overlooked in immunocompetent or intermittently immunosuppressed patients. In this patient, immune dysregulation due to underlying RA and advanced age likely contributed to HSV dissemination and bone marrow suppression. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for disseminated HSV in patients with autoimmune diseases presenting with mucocutaneous lesions and cytopenias, even in the absence of significant immunosuppressive therapy. Prompt recognition and antiviral therapy are critical to prevent complications and improve outcomes.

items.title: Pulmonary Embolism Revealing an Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Venous thromboembolism presents a rare clinical manifestation of Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with polyangiitis. We present a case of pulmonary embolism associated with Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (EGPA) systemic manifestations in a 26-year-old Tunisian female patient. She presented with dyspnea and blood hypereosinophilia. Blood tests revealed elevated D-dimer levels. Lung scintigraphy (V/Q-scan) revealed pulmonary artery embolism in the right lung. The Computed Tomography (CT) image showed circumferential wall thickness of the lower mediastinal oesophagus and gastroesophageal junction. The chest scan also showed multiple pulmonary infiltrates with a ground-glass appearance localized in the apex of the posterior segment of the right upper lobe. The CT scan of the sinuses showed circumferential thickening of the maxillary sinus. Based on the 2022 ACR/EULAR diagnosis criteria, the patient was diagnosed with Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis. After one month of anti-vitamin K treatment, a spirometry showed an obstructive pattern. The patient underwent methylprednisolone pulses, followed by oral corticosteroids, which were slowly tapered concomitantly with a cyclophosphamide regimen. A marked improvement of the spirometry parameters was achieved. Clinicians should be vigilant in the diagnostic and therapeutic management of Pulmonary Embolism (PE) during the active phase of EGPA to establish adequate follow-up procedures.

items.title: A3 Adenosine Receptor in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Friend or Foe? A Key Mediator of Different Signaling Pathways.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease that has heterogeneous clinical manifestations. The A3 Adenosine Receptor (A3AR), a protein implicated in numerous inflammatory pathways, is overexpressed in patients with RA. The available preclinical and clinical literature about A3AR signaling in RA was reviewed, and published data on its molecular pathways, immunomodulatory functions, and role in synovial fibroblasts were searched. Studies exploring A3AR agonists and their mechanistic interactions with NF-κB and p53 pathways were also reviewed. The mechanisms in which the A3AR is involved in alleviating inflammatory status resulting from alterations in transcriptional activity of the nuclear factor kappa B-light- chain-enhancer of activated inflammatory cells (NF-κB) in RA and the clinical and preclinical studies working on A3AR agonists alongside the apoptosis process by interacting with the p53 expression level. In contrast, we explained that the canonical and non-canonical pathways for A3AR, which may lead to worsening inflammation, were detailed. The implication of A3AR in the worsening of destructive effects on RA synovium in cases of hypoxia, as well as the consequences of low oxygen levels on FLSs, was detailed. In conclusion, we hypothesized that the overexpressed A3AR could provide the activation of Ras, leading to the inflammatory and senescent phenotype of FLSs during the pathological processes in RA.

items.title: Integrative Bioinformatics Identifies TTN as a Potential Diagnostic Marker for Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease with heterogeneous clinical manifestations, and its molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. To identify core genes associated with RA and evaluate their diagnostic utility, with an emphasis on immune relevance and causality. Differential expression analysis and weighted gene coexpression network analysis were used to prioritize hub genes. Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction analyses supported biological interpretation. A nomogram and receiver operating characteristic analysis were used to evaluate diagnostic performance, and immune cell infiltration was analyzed to identify immune-associated core genes. The causal effect of titin on the risk of RA was estimated using genome-wide association study data and two-sample Mendelian randomization. Validation was conducted in independent public transcriptomic datasets and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of synovial tissue. Titin (TTN) was prioritized as an RA-associated core gene and demonstrated favorable diagnostic performance. TTN expression was consistently higher in RA than in controls across validation datasets. Public external validation datasets supported increased TTN expression in RA, and scRNA-seq analysis suggested enrichment of TTN expression in synovial T cells. Mendelian randomization supported a causal association between genetically predicted TTN and RA risk. Collectively, evidence from bulk transcriptomics, immune cell infiltration profiling, single-cell localization, external validation, and genetic inference supports TTN as a previously underexplored candidate RA-associated biomarker with potential immune relevance. These findings extend current RA biomarker discovery by linking diagnostic performance with immune context and genetic support. Further mechanistic studies are needed to clarify whether TTN is involved in RA immunopathology or reflects inflammation-related tissue remodeling. Integrative analyses identify TTN as a potential RA-associated diagnostic biomarker requiring further experimental and clinical validation. Further studies are needed to clarify its mechanistic role and clinical utility in RA.

items.title: The Usefulness of White Blood Cell Inflammatory Parameters in Children With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: To evaluate the utility of novel parameters related to immune cell activation, known as white blood cell parameters of inflammation (WBC-IP), as biomarkers of disease activity in childhood-onset systemic lupus erythematosus (cSLE) and compare their performance with conventional markers, including erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), and procalcitonin (PCT). We conducted a cross-sectional analysis, including patients with cSLE with active disease (n = 43), remission (n = 31), and healthy controls (n = 112). In a separate longitudinal cohort, patients with active cSLE at baseline were reassessed after four to six weeks and when achieving inactive disease. WBC-IP was measured in dipotassium EDTA-anticoagulated tubes using the Sysmex XN-Series analyzer. Associations with SLEDAI-2K, clinical SLEDAI-2K, and physician global assessment (PGA) scores were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation. Diagnostic performance for distinguishing active disease from remission was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Significant alterations in neutrophil- and lymphocyte-related parameters were observed across disease states. The proportion of immature granulocytes (IG%) correlated most strongly with the SLEDAI-2K (r s  = 0.51), clinical SLEDAI-2K (r s  = 0.50), and PGA (r s  = 0.57; all P < 0.0001) and showed comparable associations with ESR, CRP, and PCT. Longitudinal changes in IG%, neutrophil reactivity intensity, and lymphocyte complexity indices paralleled improvements in disease activity. IG% best discriminated active cSLE among WBC-IP (AUC 0.90, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.83-0.98; cutoff >0.35, sensitivity 81.4%, specificity 87.1%), whereas ESR demonstrated the highest AUC among conventional markers (AUC 0.92, 95% CI 0.85-0.99). Among the WBC-IP evaluated, IG% showed the strongest association with disease activity and demonstrated diagnostic performance comparable to that of ESR, suggesting it may represent a potential biomarker of disease activity. Further validation in independent cohorts is warranted.

items.title: Autophagy - related protein 5: A promising biomarker for disease activity and treatment response in lupus nephritis.
items.abstract: Existing biomarkers are often insufficient for adequately tracking treatment outcomes in lupus nephritis (LN). Growing evidence points to a significant role of autophagy in LN pathogenesis. This study aimed to evaluate circulating levels of autophagy-related protein 5 (ATG5) alongside its immunohistochemical expression in kidney biopsy from LN patients, and to examine its utility as a diagnostic indicator and predictor of therapeutic response. This pilot prospective research enrolled 31 patients with active LN and 9 age and sex matched normal controls. Immunohistochemical evaluation of ATG5 expression was conducted on renal biopsy specimens collected before the commencement of medication, while blood ATG5 levels were evaluated in all subjects. Serial serum ATG5 evaluations were performed at 3-month and 6-month intervals after the initiation of therapy. Circulating ATG5 levels were significantly decreased in LN patients relative to controls (cut-off ≤312.3 ng/l; AUC=0.943; sensitivity 100%; specificity 88.9%). Renal tissue ATG5 expression was detected in 96.7% of patients; strong expression identified in 87.1% using summation scoring (score >3) and in 58.1% using multiplication scoring (score >8). A biopsy summation score ≤6 predicted treatment response with AUC of 0.88, sensitivity 69.57% and 100% specificity. Treatment was associated with significant ATG5 recovery over 6 months (p < 0.001), with responders demonstrating lower biopsy scores and greater serum ATG5 improvement versus non-responders (p=0.004, p=0.009, respectively). Mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) treatment yielded superior outcomes compared to cyclophosphamide (p=0.042). The summation and multiplication scores of ATG5 exhibited a negative correlation with serum ATG5 after six months (p < 0.026 and p < 0.018, respectively). In conclusion, ATG5 represents a valuable autophagy-related biomarker in LN, offering reliable predictive utility for treatment outcomes. Lower intra-renal ATG5 expression scores are associated with favourable therapeutic responses, particularly in patients receiving MMF.

items.title: Causes of hospitalization in systemic lupus erythematosus patients at a tertiary care center: insights from South Asia.
items.abstract: Patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) often require hospitalization due to disease flares, infections, or other complications. While studies from high-income countries consistently report flares and infections as leading causes, data from South Asia remain limited. This study aimed to identify the leading causes of hospitalization and describe the associated clinical outcomes of patients admitted to a tertiary care center in Nepal. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted at the B.P. Koirala Institute of Health Sciences, Nepal, including all eligible SLE patients (aged >16 years and diagnosed for >3 months using the SLICC 2012 criteria) from November 2023 to November 2024. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and treatment data were collected. Reasons for hospitalization and in-hospital outcomes were recorded. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Sixty-four patients were included; 93.8% were female, with a mean age of 32.4 ± 11.1 years. SLE flare was the most common cause of hospitalization (56.3%), followed by infection (20.3%). Renal flare accounted for the most flare-related admissions (39.1%), while urinary tract infection and acute undifferentiated fever were the leading infections. Nearly half of the patients (46.9%) were not on any immunosuppressive therapy at admission, and hydroxychloroquine use was suboptimal (67.2%). The mean hospital stay was 5.3 ± 3.0 days. Most patients were discharged in stable condition (95.3%); one required ICU transfer, and one died (1.6%). Renal flares and infections were the most frequent causes of hospitalization in this South Asian SLE cohort, highlighting the need for early recognition and management.

items.title: Xinfeng capsule regulates pyroptosis and ameliorates cardiac fibrosis in rheumatoid arthritis through lncRNA GAS5 and TLR4/ROS/miR-21 pathways.
items.abstract: Xinfeng capsule (XFC) is a traditional Chinese medicinal compound that has been used clinically for several years to treat rheumatoid arthritis (RA)-related cardiac dysfunction. Nevertheless, the mechanism through which XFC treats RA-induced cardiac impairment remains unclear. This study investigates the mechanism by which XFC-containing serum regulates pyroptosis and ameliorates cardiac fibrosis in RA through the lncRNA GAS5 and TLR4/ROS/miR-21 pathways. A cardiac fibrosis model using human myocardial cells was established to study lncRNA GAS5, miR-21, TLR4, and NLRP3 expressions. Immunofluorescence, RT-qPCR, WB, dual-luciferase assay, CCK-8, flow cytometry, electron microscopy, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay were used to analyze various cellular processes and protein levels. Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) releases were also analyzed. The mRNA and protein expressions of multiple genes were assessed. The optimal intervention conditions for AC16 cells were determined as follows: 20 µg/L for lipopolysaccharide (LPS) for 24 h, and 10% for XFC. In the LPS group, cell viability decreased, LDH release increased, and there was an elevation in pro-inflammatory cytokines and pyroptosis-related protein expression. GAS5 expression was reduced, while TLR4, ROS, and miR-21 showed increased levels compared to the NC group. GAS5 acted as an inhibitor by sponging miR-21. Conversely, XFC-containing serum, GAS5 overexpression, and miR-21 inhibition exhibited positive effects - enhancing cell viability, preventing LDH and pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and reducing pyroptosis and fibrosis-related protein levels. XFC can inhibit cellular pyroptosis, reduce pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, and improve RA cardiac fibrosis via lncRNA GAS5 and TLR4/ROS/miR-21 pathways.

items.title: Anti-Inflammatory Effects of Vicatia thibetica De Boiss. in Rheumatoid Arthritis and Associated Multi-Pathway Modulation In Vivo.
items.abstract: Vicatia thibetica de Boiss. (VTDB) is not only used as an important Tibetan medicine but is also consumed as a common wild vegetable. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disorder characterized by persistent synovial inflammation and progressive destruction of cartilage and bone. VTDB is recorded in the Four Medical Classics for treating "Huang-Shui," a condition resembling RA. To preliminarily investigate its potential therapeutic basis, VTDB and its polarity-based fractions were evaluated for their effects against RA. The chemical constituents of VTDB-TE were profiled using UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap MS/MS, and network pharmacology analysis predicted possible involvement of the PI3K/Akt and JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathways. Among the tested fractions, VTDB-nBuOH exhibited the most pronounced pharmacological activity in the collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rat model. VTDB-nBuOH treatment was associated with reduced paw swelling, lower serum levels of rheumatoid factor (RF) and C-reactive protein (CRP), and improved synovial histopathology. The treatment was also associated with reduced levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines and alterations in the levels of proteins associated with PI3K/Akt, JAK2/STAT3, and the downstream IKK/IκB/NF-κB axis. Additionally, VTDB-nBuOH treatment was associated with a shift in macrophage polarization markers toward an anti-inflammatory M2-like phenotype, suggesting a possible restoration of the M1/M2 balance within the joint microenvironment. 16S rRNA sequencing revealed VTDB-nBuOH treatment-associated changes in gut microbial composition, including enrichment of certain beneficial genera and reduction of some pathogenic taxa. Proteomic analysis also pointed to the PI3K/Akt pathway as a potential node of interest. Collectively, these correlative findings suggest that VTDB-nBuOH may alleviate synovial inflammation and cartilage and bone damage through multi-pathway modulation, though further mechanistic studies are needed to establish causality. VTDB-nBuOH shows preliminary promise for further investigation as a potential candidate for RA treatment.
